title.zh: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲
title.en: Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun
title.raw: 卷一百二十四 載記第二十四 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲 Volume 124 Records 24: Murong Bao; Murong Sheng; Murong Xi; Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶 慕容盛 慕容熙 慕容雲

translations.literal: Murong Bao, Murong Sheng, Murong Xi, Murong Yun
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao · Murong Sheng · Murong Xi · Murong Yun

sentences.zh: 慕容寶，字道祐，垂之第四子也。

translations.literal: Murong Bao, courtesy name Daoyou, was Chui's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bao, whose courtesy name was Daoyou, was the fourth son of Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 少輕果無志操，好人佞己。

translations.literal: In youth he was light, rash, and without settled purpose; he loved men who flattered him.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reckless and fickle, with no firm principles, and he surrounded himself with flatterers.

sentences.zh: 苻堅時為太子洗馬、萬年令。

translations.literal: In Fu Jian's time he served as gentleman attendant of the heir apparent and magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Fu Jian he held the posts of gentleman attendant to the crown prince and magistrate of Wannian county.

sentences.zh: 堅淮肥之役，以寶為陵江將軍。

translations.literal: At Fu Jian's campaign at Huainan and Feishui, Bao was made general who crosses the river.
translations.idiomatic: During Fu Jian's defeat at Feishui, Bao was appointed general who crosses the Jiang.

sentences.zh: 及為太子，砥礪自修，敦崇儒學，工談論，善屬文，曲事垂左右小臣，以求美譽。

translations.literal: When he became heir apparent, he honed himself, honored Confucian learning, was skilled at discussion and literary composition, and obsequiously served Chui's attendants and petty officials to seek a good reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Once made heir apparent, he cultivated himself, promoted Confucian studies, excelled at debate and prose, and curried favor with Chui's courtiers to win praise.

sentences.zh: 垂之朝士翕然稱之，垂亦以為克保家業，甚賢之。

translations.literal: Chui's courtiers all at once praised him, and Chui also thought he could preserve the family enterprise and greatly regarded him as worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court took up the chorus; Chui believed his son could safeguard the house and held him in high esteem.

sentences.zh: 垂死，其年寶嗣偽位，大赦境內，改元為永康。

translations.literal: When Chui died, that same year Bao succeeded to the usurped throne, proclaimed a general amnesty within the borders, and changed the era name to Yongkang.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's death that year brought Bao to the throne; he amnestied the realm and proclaimed the Yongkang era.

sentences.zh: 以其太尉庫辱官偉為太師、左光祿大夫，段崇為太保，其餘拜授各有差。

translations.literal: He made his grand marshal Kuoruguan Wei grand preceptor and left grand master of the palace, Duan Chong grand guardian, and the rest received appointments each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: He named his grand marshal Kuoruguan Wei grand preceptor and left grand master of the palace, made Duan Chong grand guardian, and distributed the remaining offices by rank.

sentences.zh: 遵垂遺令，校閱戶口，罷諸軍營分屬郡縣，定士族舊籍，明其官儀，而法峻政嚴，上下離德，百姓思亂者十室而九焉。

translations.literal: Following Chui's testament, he audited households, abolished military camps and assigned them to commanderies and counties, fixed the old registers of the gentry clans, clarified official ritual, yet the laws were severe and government stern, above and below parted in virtue, and in nine houses out of ten the people thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He carried out Chui's last orders—household surveys, dismantling military camps into civil districts, fixing aristocratic registers, and clarifying court ceremony—but harsh law and stern rule estranged elites from the throne until rebellion stirred in nearly every household.

sentences.zh: 初，垂以寶塚嗣未建，每憂之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Bao had no heir established in the ancestral tomb rites, Chui had continually worried over this.
translations.idiomatic: Chui had long worried that Bao had not secured his succession with a proper heir.

sentences.zh: 寶庶子清河公會多材藝，有雄略，垂深奇之。

translations.literal: Bao's son by a concubine, Qinghe Duke Hui, was endowed with many talents and arts and possessed bold strategy; Chui deeply marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's bastard son, the Prince of Qinghe, Hui, combined many gifts with bold strategy, and Chui took him for a wonder.

sentences.zh: 及寶之北伐，使會代攝宮事，總錄、禮遇一同太子，所以見定旨也。

translations.literal: When Bao marched north, he had Hui act as regent over palace affairs, with oversight and honors equal to the heir apparent—thus showing the settled intent.
translations.idiomatic: On Bao's northern campaign he left Hui as regent with honors matching the heir apparent, a clear sign of his intended successor.

sentences.zh: 垂之伐魏，以龍城舊都，宗廟所在，復使會鎮幽州，委以東北之重，高選僚屬以崇威望。

translations.literal: When Chui attacked Wei, because Longcheng was the old capital and held the ancestral temples, he again had Hui garrison You Province and entrusted him with the weight of the northeast, selecting high officials to augment his prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's assault on Wei sent Hui back to garrison You Province—Longcheng held the imperial tombs—and loaded him with northeastern authority and handpicked aides to magnify his stature.

sentences.zh: 臨死顧命，以會為寶嗣，而寶寵愛少子濮陽公策，意不在會。

translations.literal: On his deathbed in his final charge he named Hui as Bao's successor, but Bao favored his youngest son, Puyang Duke Ce, and his mind was not on Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Chui's deathbed testament named Hui as Bao's heir, yet Bao doted on his youngest son, the Duke of Puyang, Ce, and had no heart for Hui.

sentences.zh: 寶庶長子長樂公盛自以同生年長，恥會先之，乃盛稱策宜為儲貳，而非毀會焉。

translations.literal: Bao's eldest son by a concubine, Changle Duke Sheng, regarded himself as senior by birth and was shamed that Hui should go before him; he therefore loudly praised Ce as fit for the secondary heir and slandered Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, Bao's eldest bastard, chafed at being passed over for the younger Hui and campaigned for Ce as crown prince while blackening Hui's name.

sentences.zh: 寶大悅，乃訪其趙王麟、高陽王隆，麟等咸希旨贊成之。

translations.literal: Bao was greatly pleased and thereupon consulted Princes of Zhao and Gaoyang, Lin and Long; Lin and the rest all heeded his intent and praised the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was delighted and consulted Murong Lin and Murong Long, who eagerly seconded the proposal.

sentences.zh: 寶遂與麟等定計，立策母段氏為皇后，策為皇太子，盛、會進爵為王。

translations.literal: Bao then with Lin and the others settled the plan, made Ce's mother Lady Duan empress, Ce crown prince, and advanced Sheng and Hui in rank to princes.
translations.idiomatic: With Lin's backing, Bao made Ce's mother Lady Duan empress, named Ce crown prince, and elevated Sheng and Hui to princely rank.

sentences.zh: 策字道符，年十一，美姿貌，而蠢弱不慧。

translations.literal: Ce, courtesy name Daofu, was eleven years old, of fine appearance, yet dull, weak, and without wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Ce, whose courtesy name was Daofu, was eleven—handsome but feeble-minded and witless.

sentences.zh: 魏伐并州，驃騎農逆戰，敗績，還于晉陽，司馬慕輿嵩閉門距之。

translations.literal: When Wei attacked Bing Province, the quick cavalry commander Nong met them in battle and was defeated; returning to Jinyang, the marshal Murong Song shut the gates and barred him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's invasion of Bing Province routed Murong Nong; when he retreated to Jinyang, Marshal Murong Song locked him out.

sentences.zh: 農率騎數千奔歸中山，行及潞川，為魏追軍所及，餘騎盡沒，單馬遁還。

translations.literal: Nong led several thousand horsemen in flight back to Zhongshan; on reaching Luchuan he was overtaken by Wei's pursuit—his remaining riders were all lost, and he escaped back alone on a single horse.
translations.idiomatic: Nong fled toward Zhongshan with a few thousand cavalry but was run down at Luchuan; his escort was wiped out and he rode home alone.

sentences.zh: 寶引群臣於東堂議之。

translations.literal: Bao convened the ministers in the Eastern Hall to deliberate on it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao gathered his ministers in the Eastern Hall for counsel.

sentences.zh: 中山尹苻謨曰：「魏軍強盛，千里轉鬥，乘勝而來，勇氣兼倍，若逸騎平原，形勢彌盛，殆難為敵，宜度險距之。

translations.literal: Zhongshan intendant Fu Mo said, "Wei's forces are powerful; they have fought a thousand li and come on the crest of victory with courage doubled. If they range cavalry on the plain the situation will be stronger still, and we will scarcely be able to face them—we should use perilous ground to hold them off.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Mo, intendant of Zhongshan, argued: "Wei is strong; its army has fought a thousand miles and arrives flushed with victory. On open ground their horsemen will be unstoppable—we must meet them in defensible terrain."

sentences.zh: 」中書令晆邃曰：「魏軍多騎，師行剽銳，馬上齎糧，不過旬日。

translations.literal: " Chief minister of the Secretariat Qi Sui said, "Wei has many cavalry; their columns move with raiding speed, carrying grain on horseback—no more than ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Sui replied: "Wei relies on cavalry that raid in lightning strikes and carry provisions on horseback—they cannot last ten days."

sentences.zh: 宜令郡縣聚千家為一堡，深溝高壘，清野待之。

translations.literal: We should order the commanderies and counties to gather a thousand households into one fort, dig deep moats and raise high ramparts, and clear the countryside to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Let every district mass a thousand households into walled forts, dig deep ditches, build high walls, and strip the countryside bare to starve them out."

sentences.zh: 至無所掠，資食無出，不過六旬，自然窮退。

translations.literal: When they have nothing to plunder and no supplies to draw on, in no more than sixty days they will naturally withdraw in exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: Without loot or forage they will break within sixty days."

sentences.zh: 」尚書封懿曰：「今魏師十萬，天下之勍敵也。

translations.literal: " Minister Feng Yi said, "Now Wei's army numbers a hundred thousand—the fiercest foe under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi objected: "Wei fields a hundred thousand men, the strongest army in the realm."

sentences.zh: 百姓雖欲營聚，不足自固，是則聚糧集兵以資強寇，且動眾心，示之以弱，阻關距戰，計之上也。

translations.literal: Though the people wish to gather in forts, they are not enough to defend themselves; that would only pile grain and troops to strengthen the enemy, stir popular fear, and show weakness. Blocking the passes and fighting at the frontier is the best plan.
translations.idiomatic: The people cannot hold such forts; massing grain and soldiers would only feed the invader, spread panic, and advertise weakness. We should bar the passes and give battle—that is the superior strategy."

sentences.zh: 」慕容麟曰：「魏今乘勝氣銳，其鋒不可當，宜自完守設備，待其弊而乘之。

translations.literal: " Murong Lin said, "Wei now rides the tide of victory with sharp morale; its edge cannot be met—we should complete our defenses and wait for their exhaustion, then strike when they falter.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Lin urged: "Wei comes drunk on victory; we cannot meet that edge head-on. Fortify, hoard grain, and strike only when they weaken."

sentences.zh: 」於是修城積粟，為持久之備。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they repaired the walls and amassed grain, making preparations for a prolonged defense.
translations.idiomatic: They repaired the walls, stockpiled grain, and settled in for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 魏攻中山不克，進據博陵魯口，諸將望風奔退，郡縣悉降于魏，寶聞魏有內難，乃盡眾出距，步卒十二萬，騎三萬七千，次於曲陽柏肆。

translations.literal: Wei attacked Zhongshan without success, advanced and held Boling Lukou; the generals fled at the sight of them, and the commanderies and counties all surrendered to Wei. Bao heard that Wei had internal troubles and then led his entire host out to resist—one hundred twenty thousand foot soldiers and thirty-seven thousand cavalry—and halted at Quyang Baixi.
translations.idiomatic: Wei failed to take Zhongshan but seized Boling Lukou; commanders fled and districts surrendered. Hearing of turmoil within Wei, Bao marched out with his full strength—120,000 infantry and 37,000 horse—and camped at Quyang Baixi.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進至新梁。

translations.literal: Wei's army advanced to Xinliang.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei host moved up to Xinliang.

sentences.zh: 寶憚魏師之銳，乃遣征北隆夜襲魏軍，敗績而還。

translations.literal: Bao feared the sharpness of Wei's troops and sent the northern campaign commander Long to raid Wei's camp by night; he was defeated and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Wei's edge, Bao sent Murong Long on a night attack; Long was beaten back.

sentences.zh: 魏軍方軌而至，對營相持，上下兇懼，三軍奪氣。

translations.literal: Wei's army came on in steady columns; the camps faced each other, and above and below were filled with dread—the three armies lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wei advanced in ordered ranks; the armies faced each other across the lines, and dread spread until the whole host lost its nerve.

sentences.zh: 農、麟勸寶還中山，乃引歸。

translations.literal: Nong and Lin urged Bao to return to Zhongshan, and he thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Lin persuaded Bao to fall back on Zhongshan, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 魏軍追擊之，寶、農等棄大軍，率騎二萬奔還。

translations.literal: Wei's army pursued them; Bao, Nong, and the others abandoned the great host and led twenty thousand cavalry in flight back.
translations.idiomatic: Wei gave chase; Bao and Nong abandoned the main army and fled north with twenty thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 時大風雪，凍死者相枕於道。

translations.literal: At that time a great wind and snow blew; those who froze to death lay pillow to pillow along the road.
translations.idiomatic: A blizzard swept the retreat; the dead lay heaped along the road.

sentences.zh: 寶恐為魏軍所及，命去袍杖戎器，寸刃無返。

translations.literal: Bao feared being overtaken by Wei's army and ordered robes, staves, and weapons cast away—not a blade was to return.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing capture, Bao ordered his men to discard robes, staffs, and arms until not a weapon remained.

sentences.zh: 魏軍進攻中山，屯于芳林園。

translations.literal: Wei's army advanced to attack Zhongshan and encamped at Fanglin Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Wei pressed Zhongshan and pitched camp in Fanglin Garden.

sentences.zh: 其夜尚書慕容皓謀殺寶，立慕容麟。

translations.literal: That night the minister of the Secretariat Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and install Murong Lin.
translations.idiomatic: That night Minister Murong Hao plotted to kill Bao and raise Murong Lin.

sentences.zh: 皓妻兄蘇泥告之，寶使慕容隆收皓，皓與同謀數十人斬關奔魏。

translations.literal: Hao's wife's elder brother Su Ni reported it; Bao sent Murong Long to arrest Hao. Hao and several dozen fellow conspirators cut through the gate and fled to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ni, Hao's brother-in-law, betrayed the plot; Bao sent Murong Long to seize Hao, but Hao and dozens of conspirators broke out and fled to Wei.

sentences.zh: 麟懼不自安，以兵劫左衛將軍、北地王精，謀率禁旅弑寶。

translations.literal: Lin, in fear for himself, took troops and seized the left guard general, Prince of Beidi Jing, plotting to lead the palace guard to assassinate Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, terrified, seized Prince Jing of Beidi, commander of the left guard, and plotted to murder Bao with the palace troops.

sentences.zh: 精以義距之，麟怒，殺精，出奔丁零。

translations.literal: Jing resisted on grounds of righteousness; Lin in anger killed Jing and fled to the Dingling.
translations.idiomatic: Jing refused on principle; Lin slew him in rage and fled to the Dingling.

sentences.zh: 初，寶聞魏之來伐也，使慕容會率幽、并之眾赴中山，麟既叛，寶恐其逆奪會軍，將遣兵迎之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Bao heard that Wei was coming to attack, he had Murong Hui lead the hosts of You and Bing to hurry to Zhongshan. After Lin rebelled, Bao feared Hui would seize the army in revolt and was about to send troops to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei invaded, Bao had summoned Murong Hui from You and Bing; after Lin's revolt he feared Hui would turn the army against him and prepared to intercept him.

sentences.zh: 麟侍郎段平子自丁零奔還，說麟招集丁零，軍眾甚盛，謀襲會軍，東據龍城。

translations.literal: Lin's attendant Duan Pingzi fled back from the Dingling and reported that Lin was gathering Dingling forces in great numbers, planning to strike Hui's army and seize Longcheng in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Pingzi, Lin's aide, escaped from the Dingling and warned that Lin was rallying them in force to crush Hui and seize Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 寶與其太子策及農、隆等萬餘騎迎會於薊，以開封公慕容詳守中山。

translations.literal: Bao with his crown prince Ce and Nong, Long, and more than ten thousand cavalry went to meet Hui at Ji, leaving Duke of Kaifeng Murong Xiang to hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rode out with Ce, Nong, and Long and over ten thousand cavalry to meet Hui at Ji, leaving Murong Xiang to defend Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會傾身誘納，繕甲厲兵，步騎二萬，列陣而進，迎寶薊南。

translations.literal: Hui devoted himself to winning men over, repaired armor and sharpened weapons, and with twenty thousand foot and horse advanced in battle array to welcome Bao south of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Hui worked every tie, drilled his troops, and marched south of Ji with twenty thousand men in battle order to receive Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶分其兵給農，隆，遣西河公庫辱官驥率眾三千助守中山。

translations.literal: Bao divided troops between Nong and Long and sent Duke of Xihe Kuoruguan Ji with three thousand men to help hold Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Bao split his force between Nong and Long and sent Kuoruguan Ji of Xihe with three thousand men to reinforce Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 會以策為太子，有恨色。

translations.literal: When Hui learned that Ce had been made crown prince, he showed resentment on his face.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Ce was crown prince, Hui could not hide his bitterness.

sentences.zh: 寶以告農、隆，俱曰：「會一年少，專任方事，習驕所致，豈有他也。

translations.literal: Bao told Nong and Long; both said, "Hui is still young and holds sole authority in the regions—this is the arrogance of habit; there is nothing else to it.
translations.idiomatic: Bao confided in Nong and Long; both said, "Hui is young and commands the frontier alone—his pride is only the habit of power, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 臣當以禮責之。

translations.literal: We shall rebuke him with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: We will bring him to heel with proper ceremony.

sentences.zh: 」幽平之士皆懷會威德，不樂去之，咸請曰：「清河王天資神武，權略過人，臣等與之誓同生死，感王恩澤，皆勇氣自倍。

translations.literal: " The gentlemen of You and Ping all cherished Hui's prestige and virtue and were unwilling to leave him; they all petitioned, saying, "The Prince of Qinghe is gifted by Heaven with divine martial prowess and strategy beyond other men; we have sworn with him to live and die together, and feeling his grace we are each redoubled in courage.
translations.idiomatic: Officers of You and Ping, devoted to Hui, petitioned: "The Prince of Qinghe is heaven-sent in war and counsel; we have pledged our lives to him, and under his favor our courage has doubled."

sentences.zh: 願陛下與皇太子、諸王止駕薊宮，使王統臣等進解京師之圍，然後奉迎車駕。

translations.literal: We beg Your Majesty, the crown prince, and the princes to halt at the Ji palace and let the prince lead us to raise the siege of the capital, and afterward we shall escort the imperial carriage back.
translations.idiomatic: Let Your Majesty, the crown prince, and the princes remain at Ji while the prince leads us to lift the siege of the capital; then we shall escort you home."

sentences.zh: 」寶左右皆害其勇略，譖而不許，眾咸有怨言。

translations.literal: " Bao's attendants all feared Hui's valor and strategy; they slandered him and would not consent, and the multitude all murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's courtiers, fearing Hui's talent, blocked the plan with slander, and the soldiers grumbled.

sentences.zh: 左右勸寶殺會，侍御史仇尼歸聞而告會曰：「左右密謀如是，主上將從之。

translations.literal: His attendants urged Bao to kill Hui; the attendant censor Qiuni Gui heard of it and told Hui, saying, "Those at your side are secretly plotting thus; the sovereign will follow them.
translations.idiomatic: Courtiers urged Bao to kill Hui; Qiuni Gui warned Hui: "Your father's men are plotting murder, and the emperor will listen."

sentences.zh: 大王所恃唯父母也，父已異圖；

translations.literal: What the great king relies on is only his parents—and the father already harbors a different design;
translations.idiomatic: You trust only your parents, and your father has already turned against you;

sentences.zh: 所杖者兵也，兵已去手，進退路窮，恐無自全之理。

translations.literal: what you lean on is arms, and arms have already left your hand; advance and retreat have no road, and I fear there is no way to preserve yourself.
translations.idiomatic: your strength was your army, and that army is gone. With no path forward or back, you cannot survive."

sentences.zh: 盍誅二王，廢太子，大王自處東宮，兼領將相，以匡社稷。

translations.literal: Why not kill the two princes, depose the crown prince, and let the great king take the eastern palace himself while also holding the posts of general and minister to set the altars right?
translations.idiomatic: Slay the two princes, remove the crown prince, take the heir's place yourself, and command both army and state—that is how you save the dynasty."

sentences.zh: 」會不從。

translations.literal: " Hui did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Hui refused."

sentences.zh: 寶謂農、隆曰：「觀會為變，事當必然，宜早殺之。

translations.literal: Bao said to Nong and Long, "Seeing Hui's intent to rebel, the matter is surely so—we ought to kill him early.
translations.idiomatic: Bao told Nong and Long, "Hui means to rebel; we must kill him now."

sentences.zh: 不爾，恐成大禍。

translations.literal: If not, I fear a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise disaster will follow."

sentences.zh: 」農曰：「寇賊內侮，中州紛亂，會鎮撫舊都，安眾寧境，及京師有難，萬里星赴，威名之重，可以振服戎狄。

translations.literal: " Nong said, "Bandits and enemies trouble us within; the central provinces are in turmoil. Hui pacifies the old capital and settles the people and secures the borders; when the capital is in peril he hurries a thousand li like a shooting star—his weight in prestige can awe the Rong and Di.
translations.idiomatic: Nong objected: "Enemies press within and the heartland is in chaos. Hui holds Longcheng, calms the northeast, and when the capital calls he races a thousand li—his name alone can awe the barbarians."

sentences.zh: 又逆跡未彰，宜且隱忍。

translations.literal: Moreover his rebellious tracks are not yet clear; we ought for now to endure in concealment.
translations.idiomatic: His treason is not yet proven; we should endure a while longer."

sentences.zh: 今社稷之危若綴旒然，復內相誅戮，有損威望。

translations.literal: Now the peril to the altars hangs by a single thread; to kill kin within would harm our prestige.
translations.idiomatic: The state hangs by a thread; fratricide now would only shatter what authority we have left."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「會逆心已成，而王等仁慈，不欲去之，恐一旦釁發，必先害諸父，然後及吾。

translations.literal: " Bao said, "Hui's rebellious heart is already formed, yet you kings are benevolent and unwilling to remove him; I fear that once trouble breaks out he will first harm the princes, then reach me.
translations.idiomatic: Bao said, "Hui's treason is set, yet you are too merciful to act. When the blow falls he will kill your kin first, then me."

sentences.zh: 事敗之後，當思朕言。

translations.literal: After the affair fails, you will think of my words.
translations.idiomatic: When it is too late, remember what I told you."

sentences.zh: 」農等固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: " Nong and the others firmly remonstrated, and he thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Nong and Long pressed him until he relented."

sentences.zh: 會聞之彌懼，奔于廣都黃榆穀。

translations.literal: When Hui heard of this he was all the more afraid and fled to Guangdu Huangyu Valley.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, terrified, fled to Huangyu Valley at Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 會遣仇尼歸等率壯士二千餘人分襲農、隆，隆是夜見殺，農中重創。

translations.literal: Hui sent Qiuni Gui and others with more than two thousand stalwarts to strike Nong and Long in separate attacks; Long was killed that night, and Nong was gravely wounded.
translations.idiomatic: Hui sent Qiuni Gui with two thousand men to strike Nong and Long; Long died that night and Nong was badly wounded.

sentences.zh: 既而會歸於寶，寶意在誅會，誘而安之，潛使左衛慕輿騰斬會，不能傷。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Hui returned to Bao; Bao intended to execute Hui, lured him with reassurances, and secretly sent the left guard Murong Teng to behead Hui—but could not wound him.
translations.idiomatic: Hui then came back to Bao, who meant to kill him, soothed him with false kindness, and set Murong Teng to cut him down—yet Teng could not harm him.

sentences.zh: 會復奔其眾，於是勒兵攻寶。

translations.literal: Hui again fled to his troops, and thereupon he marshaled the army to attack Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Hui fled to his soldiers and turned them against Bao.

sentences.zh: 寶率數百騎馳如龍城，會率眾追之，遣使請誅左右佞臣，並求太子，寶弗許。

translations.literal: Bao led several hundred cavalry in gallop toward Longcheng; Hui led his host in pursuit and sent envoys asking that the flattering ministers at Bao's side be executed and the crown prince demanded as well—Bao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Bao raced for Longcheng with a few hundred horsemen; Hui pursued and demanded the execution of Bao's favorites and the surrender of the crown prince—Bao refused.

sentences.zh: 會圍龍城，侍御郎高雲夜率敢死士百餘人襲會，敗之，眾悉逃散，單馬奔還中山，乃逾圍而入，為慕容詳所殺。

translations.literal: Hui besieged Longcheng; the attendant Gentleman Gao Yun by night led more than a hundred dare-to-die men to strike Hui, defeated him, and his host all scattered in flight; he alone on a single horse fled back to Zhongshan, crossed the siege lines to enter, and was killed by Murong Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Hui besieged Longcheng until Gao Yun led a hundred dare-to-die men in a night attack, routed him, and scattered his army; Hui rode alone to Zhongshan, slipped through the lines, and Murong Xiang killed him.

sentences.zh: 詳僭稱尊號，置百官，改年號。

translations.literal: Xiang usurped the exalted title, set up the hundred offices, and changed the era name.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Xiang seized the imperial title, appointed officials, and proclaimed a new era.

sentences.zh: 荒酒奢淫，殺戮無度，誅其王公以下五百餘人，內外震局，莫敢忤視。

translations.literal: He was dissolute in wine and extravagant in lust, killing without measure; he executed more than five hundred princes and officials from the kingly house downward, and within and without were shaken—none dared meet his gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Drunken, lecherous, and murderous without limit, he slaughtered more than five hundred royals and officials until the court trembled and no one dared look him in the eye.

sentences.zh: 城中大饑，公卿餓死者數十人。

translations.literal: Famine gripped the city; several tens of the nobility starved to death.
translations.idiomatic: Famine stalked the city, and dozens of high officials starved.

sentences.zh: 麟率丁零之眾入中山，斬詳及其親党三百餘人，復僭稱尊號。

translations.literal: Lin led the Dingling host into Zhongshan, beheaded Xiang and his intimate faction of more than three hundred, and again usurped the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: Lin entered Zhongshan with the Dingling, killed Xiang and three hundred of his kin and allies, and proclaimed himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 中山饑甚，麟出據新市，與魏師戰於義台，麟軍敗績。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was in extreme famine; Lin went out and held Xincheng, and fought Wei's army at Yitai; Lin's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Starvation wracked Zhongshan; Lin moved to Xincheng and met Wei at Yitai, where he was routed.

sentences.zh: 魏師遂人中山，麟乃奔鄴。

translations.literal: Wei's army then entered Zhongshan; Lin thereupon fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei took Zhongshan, and Lin fled to Ye.

sentences.zh: 慕容德遣侍郎李延勸寶南伐，寶大悅，慕容盛切諫，以為兵疲師老，魏新平中原，宜養兵觀釁，更俟他年。

translations.literal: Murong De sent his attendant Li Yan to urge Bao to march south; Bao was greatly pleased. Murong Sheng remonstrated earnestly, holding that the troops were weary and the army aged, Wei had newly pacified the Central Plain, and they ought to nurture their forces and watch for openings, waiting for another year.
translations.idiomatic: Murong De sent Li Yan to urge a southern campaign; Bao was elated, but Murong Sheng argued that the army was exhausted, Wei had just secured the Central Plain, and they should rest and wait for another chance.

sentences.zh: 寶將從之。

translations.literal: Bao was about to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Bao was on the point of agreeing.

sentences.zh: 撫軍慕輿騰進曰：「今眾旅已集，宜乘新定之機以成進取之功。

translations.literal: The commissioner of the army Murong Teng advanced and said, "Now the hosts are already gathered; we ought to seize the newly settled moment to accomplish the merit of advance.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Teng objected: "The troops are assembled; we must strike now while the moment is fresh and win glory."

sentences.zh: 人可使由之，而難與圖始，惟當獨決聖慮，不足廣采異同，以沮亂軍議也。

translations.literal: Men may be made to follow, but it is hard to plan the beginning with them; Your Sagely Resolve alone should decide—there is no need to gather many differing views and thereby disrupt the army's counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers can be led once the order is given, but they cannot be consulted at the start. Your Majesty must decide alone and not let debate wreck the campaign."

sentences.zh: 」寶曰：「吾計決矣，敢諫者斬！

translations.literal: " Bao said, "My plan is settled—whoever dares remonstrate shall be beheaded!
translations.idiomatic: Bao declared, "My mind is made up. Anyone who objects dies!"

sentences.zh: 」寶發龍城，以慕輿騰為前軍大司馬，慕容農為中軍，寶為後軍，步騎三萬，次於乙連。

translations.literal: " Bao set out from Longcheng, making Murong Teng grand marshal of the vanguard, Murong Nong the center army, and himself the rear army, with thirty thousand foot and horse, and halted at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Longcheng with Murong Teng leading the van, Murong Nong the center, and himself the rear—thirty thousand men—and camped at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 長上段速骨、宋赤眉因眾軍之憚役也，殺司空、樂浪王宙，逼立高陽王崇。

translations.literal: The senior soldier Duan Sugubone and Song Chimei, because the host feared corvée labor, killed the minister of works, Prince of Lelang Zhou, and forced Gaoyang Prince Chong to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Sugubone and Song Chimei, exploiting the army's fear of forced labor, murdered Prince Zhou of Lelang, minister of works, and installed Prince Chong of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 寶單騎奔農，仍引軍討速骨。

translations.literal: Bao fled alone on horseback to Nong and then led the army to attack Sugubone.
translations.idiomatic: Bao rode alone to Nong and marched against Sugubone.

sentences.zh: 眾咸憚征幸亂，投杖奔之。

translations.literal: The host all feared the campaign and mutiny; they cast aside their staves and fled to join the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The soldiers dreaded another march; they threw down their weapons and joined the mutineers.

sentences.zh: 騰眾亦潰，寶、農馳還龍城。

translations.literal: Teng's host also collapsed; Bao and Nong galloped back to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Teng's force dissolved as well; Bao and Nong fled back to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗潛與速骨通謀，速骨進師攻城，農為蘭汗所譎，潛出赴賊，為速骨所殺。

translations.literal: Lan Han secretly plotted with Sugubone; Sugubone advanced to attack the city. Nong was deceived by Lan Han, slipped out secretly to join the rebels, and was killed by Sugubone.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han conspired with Sugubone, who besieged Longcheng; Nong, tricked by Lan Han, slipped out to the rebels and was killed.

sentences.zh: 眾皆奔散，寶與慕容盛、慕輿騰等南奔。

translations.literal: The host all scattered in flight; Bao fled south with Murong Sheng, Murong Teng, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: The army broke apart; Bao fled south with Sheng, Teng, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 蘭汗奉太子策承制，遣使迎寶，及於薊城。

translations.literal: Lan Han supported the crown prince Ce to hold the government by imperial order and sent envoys to welcome Bao; they met him at Ji city.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han set Ce up as regent and sent envoys to welcome Bao, meeting him at Ji.

sentences.zh: 寶欲還北，盛等咸以汗之忠款虛實未明，今單馬而還，汗有貳志者，悔之無及。

translations.literal: Bao wished to return north; Sheng and the others all held that Han's loyalty and sincerity, true or false, were not yet known, and that if he went back alone on horseback, should Han harbor a divided heart, there would be no time for regret.
translations.idiomatic: Bao wanted to go north, but Sheng warned that Lan Han's loyalty was untested and a lone rider returning north would have no escape if Han turned false.

sentences.zh: 寶從之，乃自薊而南。

translations.literal: Bao followed this and thereupon went south from Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Bao took their advice and turned south from Ji.

sentences.zh: 至黎陽，聞慕容德稱制，懼而退。

translations.literal: When he reached Liyang he heard that Murong De had assumed regency and, in fear, withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: At Liyang he learned Murong De had taken power and retreated in alarm.

sentences.zh: 遣慕輿騰招集散兵于钜鹿，慕容盛結豪桀于冀州，段儀、段溫收部曲于內黃，眾皆響會，克期將集。

translations.literal: He sent Murong Teng to gather scattered troops at Julu; Murong Sheng rallied bold men in Ji Province; Duan Yi and Duan Wen gathered their followings at Neihuang—the multitude all responded and fixed a day to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Teng to rally broken units at Julu, Sheng to gather champions in Ji, and Duan Yi and Duan Wen to raise their bands at Neihuang; men answered from every side and set a date to rise.

sentences.zh: 會蘭汗遣左將軍蘇超迎寶，寶以汗垂之季舅，盛又汗之壻也，必謂忠款無貳，乃還至龍城。

translations.literal: It happened that Lan Han sent the left general Su Chao to welcome Bao; Bao, because Han was Chui's youngest uncle by the mother's line and Sheng was Han's son-in-law, was certain there could be no divided loyalty, and returned to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han sent Su Chao to escort him home; trusting Han as Chui's uncle and Sheng's father-in-law, Bao believed him loyal and returned to Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 汗引寶入于外邸，弑之，時年四十四，在位三年，即隆安三年也。

translations.literal: Han led Bao into the outer residence and assassinated him; he was forty-four years old, had held the throne three years, in the third year of Longan.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han received him in the outer palace and murdered him. Bao was forty-four, had reigned three years, in Longan year three.

sentences.zh: 汗又殺其太子策及王公卿士百餘人。

translations.literal: Han also killed the crown prince Ce and more than a hundred princes, dukes, and ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He also killed Crown Prince Ce and more than a hundred royals and officials.

sentences.zh: 汗自稱大都督、大將軍、大單于、昌黎王。

translations.literal: Han styled himself area commander-in-chief, grand general, grand chanyu, and Prince of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han proclaimed himself area commander-in-chief, grand general, grand chanyu, and Prince of Changli.

sentences.zh: 盛僭位，偽諡寶惠湣皇帝，廟號烈宗。

translations.literal: Sheng usurped the exalted throne, falsely posthumously titled Bao as Emperor Huimin, with temple name Liezong.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng seized the throne and gave Bao the posthumous title Emperor Huimin and the temple name Liezong.

sentences.zh: 皝之遷于龍城也，植松為社主。

translations.literal: When Huang moved the capital to Longcheng, he planted pines as the lord of the soil altar.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang's removal to Longcheng included planting pines to serve as tutelary trees at the altar of the soil.

sentences.zh: 及秦滅燕，大風吹拔之。

translations.literal: When Qin destroyed Yan, a great wind uprooted them.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's conquest of Yan brought a gale that tore the pines from the ground.

sentences.zh: 後數年，社處忽有桑二根生焉。

translations.literal: Some years later, two mulberry roots suddenly grew at the altar site.
translations.idiomatic: Years afterward, two mulberry shoots appeared without warning where the altar had stood.

sentences.zh: 先是，遼川無桑，及廆通于晉，求種江南，平州桑悉由吳來。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liaochuan had had no mulberry; when Huang opened relations with Jin, he sought seed from Jiangnan, and all mulberry in Ping Province came from Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Liaochuan once grew no mulberry; Huang's ties with Jin brought Jiangnan stock, and every mulberry tree in Ping Province traced its line to Wu.

sentences.zh: 廆終而垂以吳王中興，寶之將敗，大風又拔其一。

translations.literal: When Huang died, Chui rose with the restoration of the Wu king; when Bao was about to fall, a great wind again uprooted one of the mulberries.
translations.idiomatic: Huang's death gave way to Chui and the Wu king's revival; on the eve of Bao's ruin, another gale ripped one mulberry away.

sentences.zh: 盛字道運，寶之庶長子也。

translations.literal: Sheng, courtesy name Daoyun, was Bao's eldest son by a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, whose courtesy name was Daoyun, was the eldest bastard son of Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 少沈敏，多謀略。

translations.literal: In youth he was deep and keen, full of stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was reserved and sharp-minded, with a head full of schemes.

sentences.zh: 苻堅誅慕容氏，盛潛奔於沖。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian executed the Murong clan, Sheng secretly fled to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Jian's purge of the Murong house sent Sheng into hiding with Murong Chong.

sentences.zh: 及沖稱尊號，有自得之志，賞罰不均，政令不明。

translations.literal: When Chong assumed the exalted title, he was self-satisfied; rewards and punishments were uneven and government orders unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Once Chong proclaimed himself emperor, he grew complacent, meting out arbitrary rewards and punishments while his government drifted without clear direction.

sentences.zh: 盛年十二，謂叔父柔曰：「今中山王智不先眾，才不出下，恩未施人，先自驕大，以盛觀之，鮮不覆敗。

translations.literal: At twelve Sheng told his uncle Rou, "The Prince of Zhongshan is not wiser than the multitude, his talent does not excel his inferiors, and he has shown no grace to men yet already holds himself high—in my view, few escape ruin.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve he told his uncle Rou, "Our Prince of Zhongshan is no smarter than the crowd, no abler than his subordinates, and already drunk on pride before he has won anyone's loyalty. I do not see how he avoids disaster."

sentences.zh: 」俄而沖為段木延所殺，盛隨慕容永東如長子，謂柔曰：「今崎嶇於鋒刃之間，在疑忌之際，愚則為人所猜，智則危甚巢幕，當如鴻鵠高飛，一舉萬里，不可坐待罟網也。

translations.literal: " Before long Chong was killed by Duan Muyan; Sheng followed Murong Yong east to Zhangzi and told Rou, "We are now jolted between blades and caught in suspicion—if foolish, one is suspected; if wise, one is in danger like a nest under a curtain. We should soar like wild geese ten thousand li in one flight and not sit waiting for the net."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chong fell to Duan Muyan. Sheng went east with Murong Yong to Zhangzi and said to Rou, "We are caught between swords and watched with distrust. Play the fool and they will suspect you; play the wise man and you hang by a thread. We must rise like geese and flee ten thousand li—not wait here to be netted."

sentences.zh: 」於是與柔及弟會間行東歸於慕容垂。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he traveled secretly east with Rou and his brother Hui to return to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He slipped away with Rou and his brother Hui and made his way back to Murong Chui in the east.

sentences.zh: 遇盜陝中，盛曰：「我六尺之軀，入水不溺，在火不焦，汝欲當吾鋒乎！

translations.literal: They met bandits in the Tong Pass; Sheng said, "My six-foot frame does not drown in water or burn in fire—do you wish to face my edge?
translations.idiomatic: Bandits waylaid them in the Tong Pass. Sheng called out, "This body of mine does not drown in water or burn in fire. Do you mean to test my blade?"

sentences.zh: 試豎爾手中箭百步，我若中之，宜慎爾命，如其不中，當束身相授。

translations.literal: Try setting up your arrow in hand at a hundred paces—if I hit it, guard your life; if I miss, I will bind myself and submit to you.
translations.idiomatic: Plant your arrow a hundred paces off. If I strike it, spare your lives. If I miss, I am yours to bind and take."

sentences.zh: 」盜用豎箭，盛一發中之。

translations.literal: " The bandits set up the arrow; Sheng with one shot hit it.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits set the target; Sheng loosed once and struck true.

sentences.zh: 盜曰：「郎貴人之子，故相試耳。

translations.literal: The bandits said, "Young master, you are a nobleman's son—we were only testing you.
translations.idiomatic: They said, "Young lord, you are clearly a nobleman's son. We were only trying you."

sentences.zh: 」資而遣之。

translations.literal: " They gave him supplies and sent him on.
translations.idiomatic: They furnished him with provisions and let him go.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，永誅俊、垂之子孫，男女無遺。

translations.literal: After more than a year Yong executed Jun and all of Chui's descendants, men and women, none spared.
translations.idiomatic: A year later Murong Yong slaughtered Murong Jun and every descendant of Murong Chui, male and female, without exception.

sentences.zh: 盛既至，垂問以西事，畫地成圖。

translations.literal: When Sheng arrived, Chui questioned him on western affairs and drew a map on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Chui, Sheng was questioned about the west and sketched the terrain in the dust.

sentences.zh: 垂笑曰：「昔魏武撫明帝之首，遂乃侯之，祖之愛孫，有自來矣。

translations.literal: Chui smiled and said, "In former days Wei Wu stroked Mingdi's head and thereupon enfeoffed him—a grandfather's love for a grandson has its origin.
translations.idiomatic: Chui smiled. "Cao Cao once stroked Cao Rui's head and made him a marquis. A grandfather's fondness for a grandson is an old story."

sentences.zh: 」於是封長樂公。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he enfeoffed him as Duke of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon created Sheng Duke of Changle.

sentences.zh: 驍勇剛毅，有伯父全之風烈。

translations.literal: Fierce, brave, firm, and resolute, he had his uncle Quan's style of valor.
translations.idiomatic: Bold, hard, and resolute, he bore the martial stamp of his uncle Murong Quan.

sentences.zh: 寶即偽位，進爵為王。

translations.literal: When Bao assumed the usurped throne, Sheng was advanced to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao took the throne, Sheng was raised to prince.

sentences.zh: 寶自龍城南伐，盛留統後事，及段速骨作亂，馳出迎衛。

translations.literal: When Bao marched south from Longcheng, Sheng was left to govern rear affairs; when Duan Suogu rebelled, he galloped out to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Bao marched south from Longcheng and left Sheng to hold the rear; when Duan Suogu rose in revolt, Sheng rode out to defend him.

sentences.zh: 寶幾為速骨所獲，賴盛以免。

translations.literal: Bao was nearly captured by Suogu; thanks to Sheng he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Bao nearly fell into Suogu's hands and was saved only by Sheng.

sentences.zh: 盛屢進奇策於寶，寶不能從，是以屢敗。

translations.literal: Sheng repeatedly offered bold stratagems to Bao, but Bao could not follow them, and so he suffered repeated defeats.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng again and again pressed daring plans on Bao, who would not heed them—and paid for it in defeat after defeat.

sentences.zh: 寶既如龍城，盛留在後。

translations.literal: After Bao reached Longcheng, Sheng remained behind.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao returned to Longcheng, Sheng stayed behind.

sentences.zh: 寶為蘭汗所殺，盛馳進赴哀，將軍張真固諫以為不可，盛曰：「我今投命，告以哀窮。

translations.literal: When Bao was killed by Lan Han, Sheng galloped in to attend the mourning; General Zhang Zhen firmly remonstrated that this could not be done. Sheng said, "I now cast my life upon him and tell him of my grief and distress.
translations.idiomatic: Lan Han murdered Bao. Sheng raced to the funeral despite Zhang Zhen's urgent warning. "I go to put my life in his hands," he said, "and plead my grief and desperation."

sentences.zh: 汗性愚近，必顧念婚姻，不忍害我。

translations.literal: Han's nature is foolish and shortsighted; he is sure to consider our marriage ties and cannot bear to harm me.
translations.idiomatic: Han is coarse and narrow-minded. He will remember we are kin by marriage and will not kill me."

sentences.zh: 旬月之間，足展吾志。

translations.literal: Within a month I shall have room enough to fulfill my purpose.
translations.idiomatic: Give me a month and I will have done what I mean to do."

sentences.zh: 」遂人赴喪。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he entered to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: He went in to mourn.

sentences.zh: 汗妻乙氏泣涕請盛，汗亦哀之，遣其子穆迎盛，舍之宮內，親敬如舊。

translations.literal: Han's wife Lady Yi wept and pleaded for Sheng; Han also pitied him, sent his son Mu to welcome Sheng, housed him in the palace, and treated him with intimate respect as before.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Yi, Han's wife, wept until Han relented. He sent his son Mu to receive Sheng, lodged him in the palace, and honored him as before.

sentences.zh: 汗兄提、弟難勸汗殺盛，汗不從。

translations.literal: Han's elder brother Ti and younger brother Nan urged Han to kill Sheng; Han would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Han's brothers Ti and Nan pressed him to kill Sheng; he refused.

sentences.zh: 慕容奇，汗之外孫也，汗亦宥之。

translations.literal: Murong Qi, Han's grandson by a daughter, Han also spared.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Qi, Han's grandson through a daughter, was spared as well.

sentences.zh: 奇入見盛，遂相與謀。

translations.literal: Qi came in to see Sheng, and together they plotted.
translations.idiomatic: Qi visited Sheng in secret, and the two began to plot together.

sentences.zh: 盛遣奇起兵於外，眾至數千。

translations.literal: Sheng sent Qi to raise troops outside; the force reached several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng sent Qi to raise an army in the countryside; within days he had several thousand men.

sentences.zh: 汗遣蘭提討奇。

translations.literal: Han sent Lan Ti to attack Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han dispatched Lan Ti against him.

sentences.zh: 提驕很淫荒，事汗無禮，盛因間之於汗曰：「奇，小兒也，未能辦此，必內有應之者。

translations.literal: Ti was arrogant, violent, lewd, and wasteful, and served Han without propriety. Sheng slandered him to Han, saying, "Qi is a small child and cannot manage this—there must be someone within responding to him.
translations.idiomatic: Ti was proud, cruel, and dissolute, and treated Han without respect. Sheng whispered to Han, "Qi is only a boy. He cannot have done this alone. Someone inside is backing him."

sentences.zh: 提素驕，不可委以大眾。

translations.literal: Ti is by nature arrogant and cannot be entrusted with a large host.
translations.idiomatic: Ti has always been insubordinate. You cannot give him a great army."

sentences.zh: 」汗因發怒，收提誅之，遣其撫軍仇尼慕率眾討奇。

translations.literal: " Han in anger arrested and executed Ti and sent his pacification-army commander Chou Nimu to lead the host against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Han flew into a rage, seized Ti, and put him to death, then sent his general Chou Nimu at the head of an army against Qi.

sentences.zh: 汗兄弟見提之誅，莫不危懼，皆阻兵背汗，襲敗慕軍。

translations.literal: Han's brothers, seeing Ti's execution, were all fearful; each held troops, turned against Han, and attacked and defeated Nimu's army.
translations.idiomatic: Han's brothers, terrified by Ti's death, took up arms against him and routed Nimu.

sentences.zh: 汗大懼，遣其子穆率眾討之。

translations.literal: Han was greatly afraid and sent his son Mu to lead troops to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Han, in panic, sent Mu with an army to crush them.

sentences.zh: 穆謂汗曰：「慕容盛，我之仇也。

translations.literal: Mu told Han, "Murong Sheng is my enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Mu told his father, "Murong Sheng is my enemy."

sentences.zh: 奇今起逆，盛必應之。

translations.literal: Qi has now risen in rebellion; Sheng is sure to respond to him.
translations.idiomatic: Qi is in open revolt. Sheng will surely join him."

sentences.zh: 兼內有蕭牆之難，不宜養心腹之疾。

translations.literal: Moreover, with trouble at the inner wall, one should not nurture a disease at the heart.
translations.idiomatic: And with rebellion at the gates, you cannot keep a viper in your bosom."

sentences.zh: 」汗將誅盛，引見察之。

translations.literal: " Han was about to execute Sheng and summoned him to observe him.
translations.idiomatic: Han resolved to kill Sheng and called him in to take his measure.

sentences.zh: 盛妻以告，於是偽稱疾篤，不復出入，汗乃止。

translations.literal: Sheng's wife informed him; he then feigned grave illness and no longer went out, and Han thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's wife warned him in time. He pretended to be deathly ill and would not leave his quarters, and Han abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 有李旱、衛雙、劉志、張豪、張真者，皆盛之舊昵，蘭穆引為腹心。

translations.literal: There were Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen—all Sheng's old intimates; Lan Mu took them as his trusted inner circle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han, Wei Shuang, Liu Zhi, Zhang Hao, and Zhang Zhen had been Sheng's close companions; Lan Mu drew them into his inner circle.

sentences.zh: 旱等屢入見盛，潛結大謀。

translations.literal: Han and the others repeatedly entered to see Sheng and secretly formed a great plot.
translations.idiomatic: They visited Sheng again and again and wove a conspiracy in secret.

sentences.zh: 會穆討蘭難等斬之，大饗將士，汗、穆皆醉。

translations.literal: When Mu attacked Lan Nan and the others and beheaded them, he held a great feast for the officers; Han and Mu were both drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Mu defeated Lan Nan and his allies and beheaded them, then feasted his officers until he and his father were drunk.

sentences.zh: 盛夜因如廁，袒而逾牆，入於東宮，與李旱等誅穆，眾皆踴呼，進攻汗，斬之。

translations.literal: Sheng at night used the excuse of going to the privy, bared his torso, climbed over the wall, entered the eastern palace, and with Li Han and the others killed Mu; the crowd all leaped and shouted; they advanced on Han and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: That night Sheng slipped out to the privy, stripped, scaled the wall, and entered the eastern palace. With Li Han and the rest he cut down Mu while the soldiers roared their assent, then stormed Han and killed him.

sentences.zh: 汗二子魯公和、陳公楊分屯令支、白狼，遣李旱、張真襲誅之。

translations.literal: Han's two sons, Duke of Lu He and Duke of Chen Yang, were stationed separately at Lingzhi and Bailang; Sheng sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen in surprise attacks to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: Han's sons He, Duke of Lu, and Yang, Duke of Chen, held Lingzhi and Bailang. Sheng sent Li Han and Zhang Zhen to strike them down.

sentences.zh: 於是內外怗然，士女咸悅，盛謙揖自卑，不稱尊號。

translations.literal: Then inside and outside were settled; men and women alike rejoiced. Sheng bowed with modest self-abasement and did not claim the exalted title.
translations.idiomatic: Peace returned within and without; the people rejoiced. Sheng refused the imperial title and received power with deliberate humility.

sentences.zh: 其年，以長樂王稱制，赦其境內，改元曰建平。

translations.literal: That year, as Prince of Changle he held government, amnestied within the borders, and changed the era name to Jianping.
translations.idiomatic: That year he ruled as Prince of Changle, proclaimed an amnesty, and adopted the era name Jianping.

sentences.zh: 諸王降爵為公，文武各復舊位。

translations.literal: All princes were reduced in rank from prince to duke; civil and military officials each resumed their former posts.
translations.idiomatic: Princes were demoted to dukes, and civil and military officers returned to their former ranks.

sentences.zh: 初，慕容奇聚眾于建安，將討蘭汗，百姓翕然從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Murong Qi had gathered troops at Jian'an intending to attack Lan Han; the people all rushed to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Murong Qi had raised forces at Jian'an to move against Lan Han, and the countryside flocked to his banner.

sentences.zh: 汗遣兄子全討奇，奇擊滅之，進屯乙連。

translations.literal: Han sent his nephew Quan to attack Qi; Qi struck and destroyed him and advanced to camp at Yilian.
translations.idiomatic: Han sent his nephew Quan against Qi, who routed him and pushed forward to encamp at Yilian.

sentences.zh: 盛既誅汗，命奇罷兵，奇遂與丁零嚴生、烏丸王龍之阻兵叛盛，引軍至橫溝，去龍城十里。

translations.literal: After Sheng had executed Han, he ordered Qi to disband; Qi then joined the Dingling Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi in holding troops and rebelling against Sheng, leading his army to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once Han was dead, Sheng ordered Qi to stand down. Instead Qi allied with the Dingling chieftain Yan Sheng and the Wuhuan king Long Zhi, marched in rebellion to Henggou ten li from Longcheng.

sentences.zh: 盛出兵擊敗之，執奇而還，斬龍、生等百餘人。

translations.literal: Sheng sent troops, defeated them, seized Qi and returned, and beheaded Long, Sheng, and more than a hundred others.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng took the field, broke the rebels, captured Qi, and executed Long, Yan Sheng, and more than a hundred of their followers.

sentences.zh: 盛於是僭即尊位，大赦殊死已下，追尊伯考獻莊太子全為獻莊皇帝，尊寶後段氏為皇太后，全妃丁氏為獻莊皇后，諡太子策為獻哀太子。

translations.literal: Sheng then usurped the exalted throne, proclaimed a great amnesty below special death, posthumously honored his father's father, Crown Prince Offered Solemn Quan, as Emperor Offered Solemn, honored Bao's consort Lady Duan as empress dowager, Quan's consort Lady Ding as empress Offered Solemn, and gave Crown Prince Ce the posthumous title Offered Lament crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng then took the imperial title, amnestied all but those guilty of capital crimes, ennobled his grandfather Murong Quan as Emperor Offered Solemn, made Bao's widow Lady Duan empress dowager and Quan's wife Lady Ding empress, and posthumously titled Crown Prince Ce Offered Lament.

sentences.zh: 盛幽州刺史慕容豪、尚書左僕射張通、昌黎尹張順謀叛，盛皆誅之。

translations.literal: Sheng's Youzhou governor Murong Hao, left vice minister of the Secretariat Zhang Tong, and Changli intendant Zhang Shun plotted rebellion; Sheng executed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Hao, governor of Youzhou, Zhang Tong, left vice minister of the Secretariat, and Zhang Shun, intendant of Changli, plotted treason; Sheng put them all to death.

sentences.zh: 改年為長樂。

translations.literal: He changed the era name to Changle.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed the era Changle.

sentences.zh: 有犯罪者，十日一自決之，無撾捶之罰，而獄情多實。

translations.literal: For criminals, every ten days they decided cases themselves; there was no beating punishment, yet prison cases were mostly true.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals were judged every ten days without corporal punishment, yet confessions were generally reliable.

sentences.zh: 高句驪王安遣使貢方物，有雀素身綠首，集於端門，棲翔東園，二旬而去，改東園為白雀園。

translations.literal: The king of Goguryeo, An, sent envoys with tribute. A sparrow with a white body and green head gathered at the Vermilion Gate, nested and flew in the eastern garden for twenty days and departed; the eastern garden was renamed White Sparrow Garden.
translations.idiomatic: King An of Goguryeo sent tribute. A white sparrow with a green head appeared at the Vermilion Gate, lingered in the eastern garden for twenty days, and flew away. Sheng renamed the garden White Sparrow Garden.

sentences.zh: 盛聽詩歌及周公之事，顧謂群臣曰：「周公之輔成王，不能以至誠感上下，誅兄弟以杜流言，猶擅美于經傳，歌德於管弦。

translations.literal: Sheng, listening to songs and the affairs of the Duke of Zhou, turned to his ministers and said, "In assisting King Cheng, the Duke of Zhou could not move those above and below with utmost sincerity; he executed his brothers to stop slander, yet still monopolizes praise in the classics and sings his virtue to pipes and strings.
translations.idiomatic: While listening to court music about the Duke of Zhou, Sheng turned to his ministers. "The Duke of Zhou could not win heaven and earth with perfect sincerity," he said. "He killed his brothers to silence rumor, yet the classics praise him and the lutes sing his name."

sentences.zh: 至如我之太宰桓王，承百王之季，主在可奪之年，二寇窺窬，難過往日，臨朝輔政，群情緝穆，經略外敷，辟境千里，以禮讓維宗親，德刑制群後，敦睦雍熙，時無二論。

translations.literal: As for my Grand Preceptor, the Prince of Huan, he inherited the age after a hundred kings, ruled when the sovereign could be displaced, with two foes watching and scheming and difficulties surpassing former days; facing court he aided government, and all hearts were gathered in harmony; outwardly he planned strategy and opened borders a thousand li; inwardly he bound the clan with ritual and courtesy and restrained the host with virtue and punishment, fostering kinship and peace, with no second opinion in the age.
translations.idiomatic: My Grand Preceptor Murong Ke inherited a broken age when the throne itself was in play, with two enemies at the gate and trials harsher than any his forebears had known. He governed the court until the realm stood firm, carried the war beyond the frontier by a thousand li, bound the royal house with ritual, ruled the nobles with law, and won such unity that no voice dissented."

sentences.zh: 勳道之茂，豈可與周公同日而言乎！

translations.literal: Can such abundant merit be spoken of in the same day as the Duke of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: His achievement—can it really be named in the same breath as the Duke of Zhou's?"

sentences.zh: 而燕詠闕而不論，盛德掩而不述，非所謂也。

translations.literal: Yet Yan's odes pass over him in silence and his great virtue is buried without record—this is not what is called for.
translations.idiomatic: Yet no ode of Yan celebrates him, and his greatness goes unrecorded. That is not as it should be."

sentences.zh: 」乃命中書更為《燕頌》以述恪之功焉。

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered the Secretariat to compose anew the "Ode of Yan" to narrate Ke's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Secretariat to compose a new "Ode of Yan" in Murong Ke's honor.

sentences.zh: 又引中書令常忠、尚書陽璆、秘書監郎敷於東堂，問曰：「古來君子皆謂周公忠聖，豈不謬哉！

translations.literal: He also summoned Secretariat Director Chang Zhong, Minister Yang Kui, and Secretariat Supervisor Lang Fu to the Eastern Hall and asked, "From antiquity gentlemen have all called the Duke of Zhou loyal and sagely—is this not absurd!
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Chang Zhong, Yang Kui, and Lang Fu to the Eastern Hall. "Men of old call the Duke of Zhou loyal and holy," he said. "Are they not mistaken?"

sentences.zh: 」璆曰：「周公居攝政之重，而能達群臣之名，及流言之謗，致烈風以悟主，道契神靈，義光萬代，故累葉稱其高，後王無以奪其美。

translations.literal: " Kui said, "The Duke of Zhou held the weight of regency yet could make known the names of the ministers; when slander spread, he brought a fierce wind to move his lord—his Way matched the spirits, his righteousness shone for ten thousand generations; therefore age after age praises his height, and later kings cannot take away his beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Kui answered, "Though he held regency, he honored his ministers by name. When slander rose, heaven sent a tempest to warn the king. His Way touched the spirits; his righteousness endures forever. That is why later ages cannot strip him of praise."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「常令以為何如？

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "Director Chang, what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Sheng asked, "Chang Zhong—what is your view?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「昔武王疾篤，周公有請令之誠，流言之際，義感天地，楚撻伯禽以訓就王德。

translations.literal: " Zhong said, "In former days, when King Wu was gravely ill, the Duke of Zhou had the sincerity of asking to die in his place; at the time when slander flowed, his righteousness moved heaven and earth; he whipped Prince Bo Qin to train and complete the king's virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "When King Wu lay dying, the Duke offered his own life in exchange. When rumor swirled, his righteousness moved heaven. He even flogged Bo Qin to teach the young king virtue."

sentences.zh: 周公為臣之忠，聖達之美，《詩》《書》已來未之有也。

translations.literal: The Duke of Zhou's loyalty as minister and the beauty of his sagely attainment—since the Odes and Documents there has been nothing like it.
translations.idiomatic: In loyalty as subject and in sagely conduct, nothing in the Odes or Documents surpasses him."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「異哉二君之言！

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "How strange are the words of you two!
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "How odd you both sound."

sentences.zh: 朕見周公之詐，未見其忠聖也。

translations.literal: I see the Duke of Zhou's deceit and have not seen his loyalty and sageliness.
translations.idiomatic: I see the Duke of Zhou's fraud, not his loyalty or his holiness."

sentences.zh: 昔武王得九齡之夢，白文王，文王曰：「我百，爾九十，吾與爾三焉。

translations.literal: In former days King Wu dreamed of the nine-year tally and told King Wen; King Wen said, "I one hundred, you ninety—I give you three of mine.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu once dreamed of the nine-year tally and told King Wen. Wen said, "I have a hundred years; you have ninety. I give you three of mine."

sentences.zh: 」及文王之終，已驗武王之壽矣。

translations.literal: " When King Wen died, King Wu's lifespan had already been verified.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen died, Wu lived out the years Wen had promised."

sentences.zh: 武王之算未盡而求代其死，是非詐乎！

translations.literal: King Wu's allotted span was not yet exhausted, yet the Duke sought to die in his place—is this not deceit!
translations.idiomatic: Wu's years were not yet spent, yet the Duke offered to die for him. Is that not deceit?"

sentences.zh: 若惑於天命，是不聖也。

translations.literal: If he was deluded about heaven's mandate, he was not sagely.
translations.idiomatic: If he misunderstood heaven's will, he was not holy."

sentences.zh: 據攝天位而丹誠不見，致兄弟之間有干戈之事。

translations.literal: He occupied the regency of heaven's throne yet his red sincerity did not appear, and between brothers there was the affair of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the throne, yet his loyalty never showed plainly—and brothers took up arms against one another."

sentences.zh: 夫文王之化，自近及遠，故曰刑于寡妻，至於兄弟。

translations.literal: King Wen's transformation extended from the near to the far; therefore it is said, "He modeled it on his wife, extending to his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen's virtue began at home and spread outward. The classic says he set the example for his wife, then for his brothers."

sentences.zh: 周公親違聖父之典而蹈嫌疑之蹤，戮罰同氣以逞私忿，何忠之有乎！

translations.literal: The Duke personally violated his holy father's canon and trod the track of suspicion; he punished those of the same breath to vent private resentment—where is the loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: The Duke broke his father's law and walked a path of suspicion. He killed his kin to satisfy private anger. Where is the loyalty in that?"

sentences.zh: 但時無直筆之史，後儒承其謬談故也。

translations.literal: Only because in that age there was no upright historian, later Confucians inherited their mistaken talk.
translations.idiomatic: There was no honest historian in his day, and later scholars repeated the legend."

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「啟金縢而返風，亦足以明其不詐。

translations.literal: " Zhong said, "Opening the golden coffer and returning the wind is also enough to show he was not deceitful.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong said, "The golden coffer and the reversing wind are proof enough that he was no fraud."

sentences.zh: 遭二叔流言之變，而能大義滅親，終安宗國，復子明辟，輔成大業，以致太平，制禮作樂，流慶無窮，亦不可謂非至德也。

translations.literal: Meeting the change of slander from the two uncles, he could yet, in great righteousness, destroy kin and in the end secure the royal house, restore the son and clarify the throne, assist in accomplishing the great enterprise, reaching peace, establishing ritual and making music, flowing blessing without end—this also cannot be called other than utmost virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When his uncles spread rumor, he destroyed kin for the sake of the state, restored the young king, finished the founding work, brought peace, and gave the realm ritual and music whose blessing has not ended. That too is the height of virtue."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「卿徒因成文而未原大理，朕今相為論之。

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "You merely follow the finished text and have not traced the great principle; I shall now argue it with you.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "You repeat what books say and never reach the root of the matter. Listen while I reason it through."

sentences.zh: 昔周自後稷積德累仁，至於文、武。

translations.literal: In former days Zhou from Hou Ji onward accumulated virtue and benevolence down to Wen and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: From Hou Ji onward the house of Zhou heaped up merit generation after generation until Wen and Wu."

sentences.zh: 文、武以大聖應期，遂有天下。

translations.literal: Wen and Wu, with great sageliness, responded to the age and thereupon possessed the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Wen and Wu answered heaven with supreme wisdom and won the realm."

sentences.zh: 生靈仰其德，四海歸其仁。

translations.literal: The living looked up to their virtue; the four seas returned to their benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: All peoples looked up to their virtue; the four seas bowed to their benevolence."

sentences.zh: 成王雖幼統洪業，而卜世修長，加呂、召、毛、畢為之師傅。

translations.literal: Though King Cheng was young in inheriting the great enterprise, the dynasty's allotted span was long to be cultivated, and Lü, Shao, Mao, and Bi were his tutors.
translations.idiomatic: King Cheng was young when he inherited the throne, yet the dynasty's fortune was long, and Lü, Shao, Mao, and Bi stood as his teachers."

sentences.zh: 若無周公攝政，王道足以成也。

translations.literal: Without the Duke of Zhou's regency, the kingly Way was enough to be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Even without the Duke's regency, the kingly Way could have been fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 周公無故以安危為己任，專臨朝之權，闕北面之禮。

translations.literal: The Duke without cause took safety and peril as his own charge, monopolized the authority of facing court, and neglected the rite of facing north.
translations.idiomatic: Without cause he made the realm's safety his private burden, seized the court's power, and ignored the rites owed a subject."

sentences.zh: 管、蔡忠存王室，以為周公代主非人臣之道，故言公將不利於孺子。

translations.literal: Guan and Cai loyally preserved the royal house, holding that the Duke's replacing the sovereign was not the Way of a minister; therefore they said the Duke would be no good for the young lord.
translations.idiomatic: Guan and Cai were loyal to the house of Zhou. They believed a minister must not replace his lord, and so they said the Duke meant harm to the boy king."

sentences.zh: 周公當明大順之節，陳誠義以曉群疑，而乃阻兵都邑，擅行誅戮。

translations.literal: The Duke ought to have made clear the great principle of obedience, set forth sincere righteousness to awaken the multitude's doubts, yet instead he blocked the army at the capital and on his own authority carried out executions.
translations.idiomatic: He should have proclaimed the law of rightful order and cleared the court's doubts with honest argument. Instead he brought troops to the capital and killed at will."

sentences.zh: 不臣之罪彰于海內，方貽王《鴟鴞》之詩，歸非於主，是何謂乎！

translations.literal: The crime of disloyalty was manifest throughout the realm; he was just then presenting the king with the ode "Owl," shifting blame onto his lord—what is this called!
translations.idiomatic: His treason was plain to the realm. He even handed the king the "Owl," laying blame on his sovereign. What do you call that?"

sentences.zh: 又周公舉事，稱告二公，二公足明周公之無罪而坐觀成王之疑，此則二公之心亦有猜于周公也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when the Duke undertook the affair, he announced it to the two dukes; the two dukes were enough to show the Duke's innocence, yet they sat watching King Cheng's doubts—this shows that in the two dukes' hearts there was also suspicion of the Duke.
translations.idiomatic: When he acted, he reported to the Duke of Shao and the Duke of Tai. They could have cleared his name, yet they watched the young king doubt him. Even they did not fully trust him."

sentences.zh: 但以疏不間親，故寄言于管、蔡，可謂忠不見於當時，仁不及于兄弟。

translations.literal: Only because the distant may not come between the close did he lodge his words in Guan and Cai—loyalty was not seen in his own day, and benevolence did not reach his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Because outsiders must not divide kin, he let Guan and Cai bear the charge. In his own time he showed no loyalty; toward his brothers he showed no kindness."

sentences.zh: 知群望之有歸，天命之不在己，然後返政成王，以為忠耳。

translations.literal: Knowing that the multitude's allegiance had a destination and heaven's mandate was not his, only then did he return government to King Cheng—this is what is called loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Only when he saw that the people's hearts had turned elsewhere and heaven no longer favored him did he hand the throne back to King Cheng. That, he would have us call loyalty."

sentences.zh: 大風拔木之征，乃皇天祐存周道，不忘文、武之德，是以赦周公之始愆，欲成周室之大美。

translations.literal: The omen of a great wind uprooting trees was heaven's blessing to preserve the Zhou way, not forgetting the virtue of Wen and Wu; thus it pardoned the Duke of Zhou's first fault, intending to perfect the Zhou house's great beauty.
translations.idiomatic: The gale that tore up trees was heaven's sign that the Zhou line still lived, that Wen and Wu were not forgotten. Heaven forgave the Duke's first transgression so the house of Zhou might reach its full glory.

sentences.zh: 考周公之心，原周公之行，乃天下之罪 人，何至德之謂也！

translations.literal: Examining the Duke of Zhou's heart and tracing the Duke of Zhou's conduct, he was a criminal under heaven—how can one call that supreme virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Weigh his heart and weigh his deeds: he was the greatest criminal of his age. What supreme virtue is there to speak of?

sentences.zh: 周公復位，二公所以杜口不言其本心者，以明管、蔡之忠也。」

translations.literal: When the Duke of Zhou returned to power, the reason the two dukes sealed their lips and did not speak their true minds was to make clear the loyalty of Guan and Cai."
translations.idiomatic: When the Duke took power again, the Duke of Shao and the Duke of Tai kept silent because they dared not speak their minds. They meant to show that Guan and Cai had been loyal."

sentences.zh: 又謂常忠曰：「伊尹、周公孰賢？

translations.literal: He also said to Chang Zhong, "Which is the worthier—Yi Yin or the Duke of Zhou?
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Chang Zhong and asked, "Between Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, which man was greater?"

sentences.zh: 」忠曰：「伊尹非有周公之親而功濟一代，太甲亂德，放于桐宮，思愆改善，然後復之。

translations.literal: " Zhong said, "Yi Yin lacked the Duke of Zhou's kinship yet his merit carried a generation; when King Taijia's virtue went astray, he was placed in the Tong Palace, reflected on his faults and improved, and only then was he restored.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong answered, "Yi Yin was no kinsman of the royal house, yet his service saved a dynasty. When King Taijia turned wicked, Yi Yin sent him to the Tong Palace until he repented and reformed, and only then brought him back."

sentences.zh: 使主無怨言，臣無流謗，道存社稷，美溢來今，臣謂伊尹之勳有高周旦。

translations.literal: He made the lord harbor no complaint and the minister bear no slander; the Way was preserved in the altars of soil and grain, and beauty overflowed to the present day—I say Yi Yin's merit towers above the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The king bore no grudge, the minister escaped blame, the state endured, and his fame shines to this day. In my view Yi Yin outshines the Duke of Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹以舊臣之重，顯阿衡之任，太甲嗣位，君道未洽，不能竭忠輔導。

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "Yi Yin, by the weight of an old minister, held the eminent office of chief minister; when Taijia succeeded, the lord's Way was not yet harmonized, and he could not exhaust loyalty in guidance and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "Yi Yin held the rank of a founding minister and the power of chief minister. When Taijia came to the throne the young king was not yet settled, and Yi Yin failed to guide him with full loyalty."

sentences.zh: 而放黜桐宮，事同夷羿，何周公之可擬乎！

translations.literal: Yet he deposed him to the Tong Palace—his act was the same as Yi of Xia's. How can he be compared to the Duke of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: Instead he cast the king into the Tong Palace, as though he were Yi the Tyrant of Xia. How is that any likeness to the Duke of Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 」郎敷曰：「伊尹處人臣之位，不能匡制其君，恐成、湯之道墜而莫就，是以居之桐宮，與小人從事，使知稼穡之艱難，然後返之天位，此其忠也。

translations.literal: " Lang Fu said, "Yi Yin stood in the position of a minister yet could not correct and restrain his lord, fearing that the way of Cheng and Tang would fall and never be achieved; therefore he placed him in the Tong Palace to associate with petty men and learn the hardship of sowing and reaping, and only then returned him to the heavenly throne—this was his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Lang Fu said, "Yi Yin could not steer his lord by counsel alone. He feared Cheng and Tang's legacy would be lost. So he sent Taijia to the Tong Palace to live among common men and learn the sweat of the fields, then restored him to the throne. That was loyalty."

sentences.zh: 」盛曰：「伊尹能廢而立之，何不能輔之以至於善乎？

translations.literal: " Sheng said, "If Yi Yin could depose and establish him, why could he not assist him to the point of goodness?
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "If Yi Yin had power to remove a king and set him back on the throne, why could he not teach him until he ruled well?"

sentences.zh: 若太甲性同桀紂，則三載之間未應便成賢後，如其性本休明，義心易發，當務盡匡規之理以弼成君德，安有人臣幽主而據其位哉！

translations.literal: If Taijia's nature were like Jie and Zhou, then within three years he should not so quickly have become a worthy successor; if his nature was originally bright and his righteous heart easy to awaken, he ought to have done his utmost in the principle of correction and guidance to assist and complete the lord's virtue—how can there be a minister who imprisons his lord and occupies his place!
translations.idiomatic: If Taijia had been another Jie or Zhou, three years would not have made a sage of him. If he was good by nature and quick to repent, Yi Yin should have corrected him on the throne, not locked him away and ruled in his place. What minister imprisons his king and sits in his seat?"

sentences.zh: 且臣之事君，惟力是視，奈何挾智藏仁以成君惡！

translations.literal: Moreover, in serving one's lord a minister looks only to exert his strength—how can one hoard wisdom and hide benevolence to complete the lord's wickedness!
translations.idiomatic: A minister serves his lord with all his strength. How can he hoard wisdom and hide kindness to let his lord grow wicked?"

sentences.zh: 夫太甲之事，朕已鑒之矣。

translations.literal: As for the affair of Taijia, I have already judged it.
translations.idiomatic: The case of Taijia is closed in my mind."

sentences.zh: 太甲，至賢之主也，以伊尹曆奉三朝，績無異稱，將失顯祖委授之功，故匿其日月之明，受伊尹之黜，所以濟其忠貞之美。

translations.literal: Taijia was a supremely worthy lord; because Yi Yin had served through three reigns without distinctive praise, he would have lost the merit of his glorious ancestor's commission; therefore he hid his sun-and-moon brightness and accepted Yi Yin's deposition, thereby fulfilling the beauty of loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia was in truth a great king. Yi Yin had served three reigns without earning praise, and would have wasted his ancestors' trust. So the king hid his own brilliance and submitted to banishment, letting Yi Yin appear loyal and true."

sentences.zh: 夫非常之人，然後能立非常之事，非常人之所見也，亦猶太伯之三讓，人無德而稱焉。

translations.literal: Only an extraordinary man can then accomplish an extraordinary deed—what an extraordinary man sees, others also, as with Taibo's three yieldings, for which men had no virtue to praise.
translations.idiomatic: Only an extraordinary man can do an extraordinary thing, and only an extraordinary man can see it. So it was with Taibo's three renunciations of the throne, which ordinary men could not call virtue."

sentences.zh: 」敷曰：「太伯三以天下讓，至仲尼而後顯其至德。

translations.literal: " Fu said, "Taibo thrice yielded the realm under heaven; only at Confucius did his supreme virtue become manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "Taibo gave up the realm three times, but his supreme virtue was not seen until Confucius praised him."

sentences.zh: 太甲受謗於天下，遭陛下乃申其美。

translations.literal: Taijia was slandered under heaven; encountering Your Majesty, his beauty is now upheld.
translations.idiomatic: Taijia was slandered throughout the realm. Only under Your Majesty is his true worth restored."

sentences.zh: 」因而談宴賦詩，賜金帛各有差。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they conversed at a banquet, composed poems, and bestowed gold and silk each in due measure.
translations.idiomatic: They feasted, exchanged poems, and received gold and silk in varying amounts."

sentences.zh: 遼西太守李郎在郡十年，威制境內，盛疑之，累征不赴。

translations.literal: Li Lang, grand administrator of Liaoxi, had been in the commandery ten years and held the borderlands in awe; Sheng grew suspicious and summoned him repeatedly, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Li Lang had ruled Liaoxi for ten years with an iron grip on the region. Sheng grew suspicious and summoned him again and again, but Lang never came."

sentences.zh: 以母在龍城，未敢顯叛，乃陰引魏軍，將為自安之計，因表請發兵以距寇。

translations.literal: Because his mother was in Longcheng, he did not dare rebel openly; he secretly drew in Wei troops as a plan for his own security and memorialized requesting to send troops to repel invaders.
translations.idiomatic: His mother still lived in Longcheng, so he would not rebel openly. He secretly courted Wei troops for protection and asked permission to raise an army against invasion."

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「此必詐也。

translations.literal: Sheng said, "This must be a ruse.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "This is surely a trick."

sentences.zh: 」召其使而詰之，果驗，盡滅其族，遣輔國將軍李旱率騎討之。

translations.literal: " He summoned Lang's envoy and interrogated him; it proved true, and he exterminated Lang's clan, dispatching the aide to the state general Li Han with cavalry to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: He called in Lang's messenger and questioned him. The plot was confirmed. Sheng wiped out Lang's clan and sent Li Han with cavalry to punish him."

sentences.zh: 師次建安，召旱旋師。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Jian'an, Sheng recalled Han to turn the army back.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Jian'an, then Sheng ordered Han to turn back."

sentences.zh: 朗聞其家被誅也，擁三千餘戶以自固。

translations.literal: Lang heard that his family had been executed and gathered more than three thousand households to fortify himself.
translations.idiomatic: Lang learned his clan had been slaughtered and rallied more than three thousand households to his defense."

sentences.zh: 及聞旱中路而還，謂有內變，不復為備，留其子養守令支，躬迎魏師于北平。

translations.literal: When he heard that Han was returning midway, he thought there was internal turmoil and no longer made preparations; he left his son Yang to hold Lingzhi and went in person to welcome Wei troops at Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Han was marching home, Lang took it for court strife and let his guard down. He left his son Yang at Lingzhi and rode north himself to meet the Wei army at Beiping."

sentences.zh: 旱候知之，襲克令支，遣廣威孟廣平率騎追朗，及於無終，斬之。

translations.literal: Han, having learned of this in advance, raided and took Lingzhi, sent the general of broad prestige Meng Guangping with cavalry to pursue Lang, caught him at Wuzhong, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Han had foreseen this. He stormed Lingzhi, sent Meng Guangping in pursuit, overtook Lang at Wuzhong, and cut off his head."

sentences.zh: 初，盛之追旱還也，群臣莫知其故。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sheng recalled Han, none of the ministers knew his reason.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first recalled Han, no minister understood why."

sentences.zh: 旱既斬朗，盛謂群臣曰：「前以追旱還者，正為此耳。

translations.literal: After Han had beheaded Lang, Sheng told the ministers, "The reason I earlier recalled Han was precisely for this.
translations.idiomatic: Once Lang was dead, Sheng told his ministers, "I recalled Han for this very reason."

sentences.zh: 朗新為叛逆，必忌官威，一則鳩合同類，劫掠良善，二則亡竄山澤，未可卒平，故非意而還，以盈怠其志，卒然掩之，必克之理也。

translations.literal: Lang had newly rebelled and was sure to fear official authority; on one hand he would gather like-minded men and plunder the good, on the other he would flee into mountains and marshes and could not quickly be pacified—therefore by returning contrary to expectation we filled and slackened his will, and by suddenly falling on him, the principle of certain victory applied.
translations.idiomatic: A fresh rebel fears the throne. He would rally allies and rob the people, or vanish into the hills. We could not finish him quickly. A sudden recall made him careless; a sudden strike was sure to win."

sentences.zh: 」群臣皆曰：「非所及也。」
