translations.literal: " The ministers all said, "Beyond what we could reach."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers said, "We would never have thought of it."

sentences.zh: 李旱自遼西還，聞盛殺其將衛雙，懼，棄軍奔走。

translations.literal: Li Han, returning from Liaoxi, heard that Sheng had killed his general Wei Shuang, was afraid, and abandoned the army and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han was returning from Liaoxi when he learned Sheng had executed his officer Wei Shuang. In fear he deserted his command and fled."

sentences.zh: 既而歸罪，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he returned to accept blame, and his rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: He soon submitted himself to judgment, and Sheng restored his titles."

sentences.zh: 盛謂侍中孫勍曰：「旱總三軍之任，荷專征之重，不能杖節死綏，無故逃亡，考之軍正，不赦之罪也。

translations.literal: Sheng said to the attendant grandee Sun Qiu, "Han bore the charge of all three armies and the weight of independent command; he could not hold his staff and die at his post but fled without cause—examined by military law, it is a crime that cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng told Sun Qiu, "Han commanded three armies on independent commission. He should have died at his post, yet he ran away without cause. By military law that is unpardonable."

sentences.zh: 然當先帝之避難，眾情離貳，骨肉忘其親，股肱失忠節，旱以刑餘之體，效力盡命，忠款之至，精貫白日。

translations.literal: Yet in the late emperor's time of refuge, popular sentiment was divided and kin forgot their kin, arms and legs lost loyal constancy; Han, with the body of one punished by mutilation, exerted strength to the end of life, and his loyal sincerity pierced the white sun.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in our father's exile the realm was torn, kin turned on kin, and loyal men were scarce. Han, though mutilated by punishment, gave his life with perfect loyalty, bright as the noon sun."

sentences.zh: 朕故錄其忘身之功，免其丘山之罪耳。」

translations.literal: I therefore record his merit of forgetting self and remit his crime as great as a hill."
translations.idiomatic: I honor what he did for us and forgive a fault as heavy as a mountain."

sentences.zh: 盛去皇帝之號，稱庶人大王。

translations.literal: Sheng removed the title of emperor and called himself the commoner great king.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laid aside the imperial title and styled himself the Great King, a man of the people."

sentences.zh: 魏襲幽州，執刺史盧溥而去。

translations.literal: Wei raided You Province and seized and carried off the inspector Lu Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Wei struck You Province, seized the inspector Lu Pu, and took him away."

sentences.zh: 遣孟廣平援之，無及。

translations.literal: He sent Meng Guangping to rescue him, but it was too late.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Meng Guangping to relieve him, but arrived too late."

sentences.zh: 盛率眾三萬伐高句驪，襲其新城、南蘇，皆克之，散其積聚，徙其五千餘戶於遼西。

translations.literal: Sheng led thirty thousand men to attack Koguryŏ, raided its Xincheng and Nansu, took both, scattered their stores, and moved more than five thousand households to Liaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng led thirty thousand men against Koguryŏ, stormed Xincheng and Nansu, seized their grain, and resettled more than five thousand households in Liaoxi."

sentences.zh: 盛引見百遼於東堂，考詳器藝，超拔者十有二人。

translations.literal: Sheng received at audience a hundred men of Liaoxi in the Eastern Hall, examined their talents and arts in detail, and elevated twelve of surpassing ability.
translations.idiomatic: In the Eastern Hall he received a hundred men from Liaoxi, tested their skills, and promoted twelve of outstanding talent."

sentences.zh: 命百司舉文武之士才堪佐世者各一人。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred offices each to recommend one civil or military man whose talent could assist the age.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered every ministry to nominate one civil or military man fit to serve the state."

sentences.zh: 立其子遼西公定為太子，大赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He established his son Ding, Duke of Liaoxi, as heir apparent and proclaimed a general amnesty short of death.
translations.idiomatic: He named his son Ding, Duke of Liaoxi, crown prince and granted a general amnesty to all but capital crimes."

sentences.zh: 宴其群臣於新昌殿，盛曰：「諸卿各言其志，朕將覽之。

translations.literal: He feasted his ministers in the Xinchang Hall; Sheng said, "Each of you, speak your ambition—I shall review them.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his ministers in the Xinchang Hall and said, "Tell me what you desire. I will hear you."

sentences.zh: 」七兵尚書丁信年十五，盛之舅子也，進曰：「在上不驕，高而不危，臣之願也。

translations.literal: " The Minister of the Seven Armies Ding Xin, fifteen years old and Sheng's nephew by marriage, advanced and said, "Not to be arrogant in high place, to be lofty yet not endangered—this is my wish.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xin, Minister of the Seven Armies, was fifteen and Sheng's nephew by marriage. He stepped forward and said, "My wish is never to grow proud in power, never to fall from a great height."

sentences.zh: 」盛笑曰：「丁尚書年少，安得長者之言乎！

translations.literal: " Sheng laughed and said, "Minister Ding is young—how does he come by an elder's words!
translations.idiomatic: Sheng laughed. "Minister Ding is young. Where did you learn an old man's counsel?"

sentences.zh: 」盛以威嚴馭下，驕暴少親，多所猜忌，故信言及之。

translations.literal: " Sheng governed subordinates with stern authority, was arrogant and violent and had few intimates, and was much given to suspicion—therefore Xin's words touched on this.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ruled by fear, was proud and harsh, trusted few, and suspected many. That was why Xin spoke as he did."

sentences.zh: 盛討庫莫奚，大虜獲而還。

translations.literal: Sheng attacked the Kumo Xi, took a great booty, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng campaigned against the Kumo Xi, won a great haul of captives and goods, and returned."

sentences.zh: 左將軍慕容國與殿中將軍秦輿、段贊等謀率禁兵襲盛，事覺，誅之，死者五百餘人。

translations.literal: The left general Murong Guo, with the palace general Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to lead the forbidden troops in a surprise attack on Sheng; the affair was discovered, and they were executed—more than five hundred dead.
translations.idiomatic: The left general Murong Guo, the palace general Qin Yu, Duan Zan, and others plotted to strike Sheng with the palace guard. The plot was found out. More than five hundred were put to death."

sentences.zh: 前將軍、思悔侯段璣、輿子興、贊子泰等，因眾心動搖，夜於禁中鼓躁大呼。

translations.literal: The former general and Marquis of Reflecting Repentance Duan Ji, Yu's son Xing, Zan's son Tai, and others, because popular hearts were shaken, at night within the forbidden quarters beat drums, raised a clamor, and shouted loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Ji, Marquis of Reflecting Repentance, Qin Yu's son Xing, Duan Zan's son Tai, and others, seeing the army waver, drummed and shouted in the palace at night."

sentences.zh: 盛聞變，率左右出戰，眾皆披潰。

translations.literal: Sheng heard of the disturbance, led his close attendants out to fight, and the crowd all scattered in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng heard the uproar, took his guard and fought. The rebels broke and fled."

sentences.zh: 俄而有一賊從暗中擊傷盛，遂輦升前殿，申約禁衛，召叔父河間公熙屬以後事。

translations.literal: Before long one rebel struck Sheng from the dark and wounded him; he was then carried in a palanquin to the front hall, tightened the forbidden guard's rules, and summoned his uncle the Prince of Hejian, Xi, to entrust him with later affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a rebel wounded him from hiding. He was carried to the front hall, tightened the palace guard, and sent for his uncle Xi, Prince of Hejian, to entrust the realm."

sentences.zh: 熙未至而盛死，時年二十九，在位三年。

translations.literal: Xi had not yet arrived when Sheng died, aged twenty-nine, having held the throne three years.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had not yet arrived when Sheng died. He was twenty-nine and had ruled three years."

sentences.zh: 偽諡昭武皇帝，墓號興平陵，廟號中宗。

translations.literal: His false posthumous title was Emperor Zhaowu; his tomb was called Xingping Mausoleum; his temple name was Zhongzong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowu, buried at Xingping Mausoleum, and honored in the ancestral temple as Zhongzong."

sentences.zh: 盛幼而羈賤流漂，長則遭家多難，夷險安危，備嘗之矣。

translations.literal: Sheng in youth was bound and cast adrift in poverty; grown, he met the family's many hardships—danger and safety, ease and peril, he tasted them all.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Sheng was cast loose in hardship. As a man he lived through every trial his house could suffer."

sentences.zh: 懲寶暗而不斷，遂峻機威刑，織芥之嫌，莫不裁之於未萌，防之於未兆。

translations.literal: Chastened by Bao's darkness and indecision, he then made severe his mechanisms and penal law; the slightest grudge, none failed to be cut off before it sprouted, guarded against before it showed.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering Bao's blindness and hesitation, he tightened law and punishment and cut off every slight before it could grow."

sentences.zh: 於是上下振局，人不自安，雖忠誠親戚亦皆離貳，舊臣靡不夷滅，安忍無親，所以卒於不免。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below were shaken and unsettled, men could not be at ease in themselves; even loyal kinsmen all turned away, old ministers were none not destroyed, cruel and without kin—therefore in the end he could not escape harm.
translations.idiomatic: Court and country trembled. No one felt safe. Loyal kin turned away, old servants were destroyed. He was ruthless even to his own, and in the end he could not escape death."

sentences.zh: 是歲隆安五年也。

translations.literal: That year was the fifth year of Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: It was the fifth year of the Long'an era."

sentences.zh: 熙字道文，垂之少子也。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Daowen, was Chui's youngest son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, whose courtesy name was Daowen, was the youngest son of Murong Chui."

sentences.zh: 初封河間王。

translations.literal: At first he was enfeoffed Prince of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was made Prince of Hejian."

sentences.zh: 段速骨之難，諸王多被其害，熙素為高陽王崇所親愛，故得免焉。

translations.literal: In the crisis of Duan Sugu's rebellion, many princes were killed by him; Xi had always been loved by the Prince of Gaoyang, Chong, and therefore escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Duan Sugu rebelled, most princes perished. Xi had long been dear to Murong Chong, Prince of Gaoyang, and so survived."

sentences.zh: 蘭汗之篡也，以熙為遼東公，備宗祀之義。

translations.literal: When Lan Han usurped, he made Xi Duke of Liaodong to fulfill the meaning of maintaining the ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Lan Han seized power, he made Xi Duke of Liaodong so the ancestral rites would not lapse."

sentences.zh: 盛初即位，降爵為公，拜都督中外諸軍事、驃騎大將軍、尚書左僕射，領中領軍。

translations.literal: When Sheng first took the throne, Xi's rank was lowered to duke; he was appointed commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, general of agile cavalry, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and head of the central guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng first ruled, Xi was reduced to duke and named commander of all armies, general of agile cavalry, left vice director of the Masters of Writing, and head of the central guard."

sentences.zh: 從征高句驪、契丹，皆勇冠諸將。

translations.literal: In campaigns against Koguryŏ and the Khitan, his courage topped all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: On campaigns against Koguryŏ and the Khitan, no general matched his courage."

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「叔父雄果英壯，有世祖之風，但弘略不如耳。」

translations.literal: Sheng said, "Uncle is heroic, resolute, and valiant, with the manner of the Founding Emperor, only his broad strategy is not equal."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "My uncle is bold and fierce, with the spirit of our founder, though his grand strategy falls short."

sentences.zh: 及盛死，其太后丁氏以國多難，宜立長君。

translations.literal: When Sheng died, his empress dowager Lady Ding, because the state had many hardships, held that a mature lord should be established.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng died, the empress dowager Lady Ding said the realm in turmoil needed an elder ruler."

sentences.zh: 群望皆在平原西元，而丁氏意在於熙，遂廢太子定，迎熙入宮。

translations.literal: The multitude's hope was all on Pingyuan Xi Yuan, but Lady Ding's intent was on Xi; she therefore deposed the heir apparent Ding and welcomed Xi into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The court favored Pingyuan Xi Yuan, but Lady Ding wanted Xi. She deposed the crown prince Ding and brought Xi into the palace."

sentences.zh: 群臣勸進，熙以讓元，元固以讓熙，熙遂僭即尊位。

translations.literal: The ministers urged him to advance; Xi yielded to Yuan, Yuan firmly yielded to Xi, and Xi thereupon usurped the exalted throne.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers pressed him to take the throne. Xi yielded to Yuan; Yuan yielded back. Xi then proclaimed himself emperor."

sentences.zh: 誅其大臣段璣、秦興等，並夷三族。

translations.literal: He executed his great ministers Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and others, and exterminated their clans to the third degree.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Duan Ji, Qin Xing, and other ministers and wiped out their clans to the third degree."

sentences.zh: 元以嫌疑賜死。

translations.literal: Yuan was granted death on suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was put to death on suspicion."

sentences.zh: 元字道光，寶之第四子也。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Daoguang, was Bao's fourth son.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, whose courtesy name was Daoguang, was the fourth son of Murong Bao."

sentences.zh: 赦殊死已下，改元曰光始，改北燕台為大單于台，置左右輔，位次尚書。

translations.literal: He pardoned all short of death, changed the era name to Guangshi, changed the Northern Yan Terrace to the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and established left and right assistants, ranking below the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He granted amnesty short of death, took the era name Guangshi, renamed the Northern Yan Terrace the Grand Chanyu Terrace, and created left and right assistants ranking below the Masters of Writing."

sentences.zh: 初，熙烝于丁氏，故為所立。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xi had taken Lady Ding as consort, and therefore was established by her.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had earlier taken Lady Ding as consort, and it was for that reason she raised him to the throne."

sentences.zh: 及寵倖苻貴人，丁氏怨恚呪詛，與兄子七兵尚書信謀廢熙。

translations.literal: When he favored the honored lady of the Fu clan, Lady Ding resented and cursed in anger and, with her brother's son the Minister of the Seven Armies Xin, plotted to depose Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When he favored Lady Fu, Lady Ding cursed him in rage and plotted with her nephew Ding Xin, Minister of the Seven Armies, to remove him."

sentences.zh: 熙聞之，大怒，逼丁氏令自殺，葬以後禮，誅丁信。

translations.literal: Xi heard of it, was greatly enraged, forced Lady Ding to kill herself, buried her with the rites due a consort, and executed Ding Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Xi learned of the plot, flew into a rage, forced Lady Ding to take her own life, buried her with the rites of a consort, and executed Ding Xin."

sentences.zh: 熙狩于北原，石城令高和殺司隸校尉張顯，閉門距熙。

translations.literal: Xi hunted on the northern plain; the magistrate of Shicheng, Gao He, killed the director of the masters of law Zhang Xian and closed the gates to resist Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was hunting on the northern plain when Gao He, magistrate of Shicheng, killed the director of the masters of law Zhang Xian and shut the gates against him."

sentences.zh: 熙率騎馳返，和眾皆投杖，熙入誅之。

translations.literal: Xi led cavalry at full gallop back; He's troops all cast aside their staves, and Xi entered and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi raced back with his horsemen. Gao He's men dropped their weapons. Xi entered the city and killed him."

sentences.zh: 於是引見州郡及單于八部耆舊於東宮，問以疾苦。

translations.literal: Thereupon he received at audience the elders of the provinces and commanderies and of the eight tribes of the Chanyu at the Eastern Palace and asked them about their hardships.
translations.idiomatic: He then received the elders of the provinces and the eight Chanyu tribes at the Eastern Palace and asked what they suffered."

sentences.zh: 大築龍騰苑，廣袤十餘里，役徒二萬人。

translations.literal: He greatly built the Longteng Park, more than ten li in breadth and length, with twenty thousand laborers.
translations.idiomatic: He built the vast Longteng Park, more than ten li across, with twenty thousand workers."

sentences.zh: 起景雲山于苑內，基廣五百步，峰高十七丈。

translations.literal: He raised Jingyun Mountain within the park, its base five hundred paces wide and its peak seventeen zhang high.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the park he raised Jingyun Mountain, five hundred paces at the base and seventeen zhang to the summit."

sentences.zh: 又起逍遙宮、甘露殿，連房數百，觀閣相交。

translations.literal: He also raised the Xiaoyao Palace and the Ganlu Hall, hundreds of connected chambers, towers and pavilions interlocking.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Xiaoyao Palace and the Ganlu Hall, hundreds of rooms linked together, towers and galleries crossing one another."

sentences.zh: 鑿天河渠，引水入宮。

translations.literal: He cut the Tianhe Canal to draw water into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He dug the Tianhe Canal to bring water into the palace."

sentences.zh: 又為其昭儀苻氏鑿曲光海、清涼池。

translations.literal: He also for his lady of splendid beauty of the Fu clan cut the Quguang Sea and the Qingliang Pool.
translations.idiomatic: For his lady Fu he carved out the Quguang Sea and the Qingliang Pool."

sentences.zh: 季夏盛暑，士卒不得休息，暍死者太半。

translations.literal: In the height of summer's heat, the soldiers could not rest; more than half died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer the laborers were given no rest. More than half died of heat."

sentences.zh: 熙游于城南，止大柳樹下，若有人呼曰：「大王且止。

translations.literal: Xi roamed south of the city and stopped under a great willow tree; it was as if someone called, "Great King, stop for now.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was touring south of the city and halted under a great willow. A voice seemed to call, "Great King, stop."

translations.literal: (Punctuation.)
translations.idiomatic: (Close of the utterance.)

sentences.zh: 」熙惡之，伐其樹，乃有蛇長丈餘，從樹中而出。

translations.literal: " Xi hated this, cut down the tree, and thereupon a serpent more than a zhang long came out from within the tree.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was angered, had the tree felled, and a serpent more than ten feet long crawled out of the trunk."

sentences.zh: 立其貴嬪苻氏為皇后，赦殊死已下。

translations.literal: He established his honored concubine of the Fu clan as empress and pardoned all short of death.
translations.idiomatic: He made his honored concubine Lady Fu empress and granted amnesty short of death."

sentences.zh: 熙北襲契丹，大破之。

translations.literal: Xi raided the Khitan in the north and inflicted a great defeat on them.
translations.idiomatic: Xi attacked the Khitan in the north and routed them."

sentences.zh: 昭儀苻氏死，偽諡湣皇后。

translations.literal: The lady of splendid beauty of the Fu clan died; her false posthumous title was Empress Min.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Fu, his lady of splendid beauty, died. She was given the posthumous title Empress Min."

sentences.zh: 贈苻謨太宰，諡文獻公。

translations.literal: He posthumously enfeoffed Fu Mo as grand preceptor with the posthumous title Duke Wenxian.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously made Fu Mo grand preceptor and Duke Wenxian."

sentences.zh: 二苻並美而豔，好微行遊宴，熙弗之禁也。

translations.literal: The two ladies Fu were both beautiful and alluring, fond of going out in disguise for pleasure and roaming; Xi did not forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: The two Fu ladies were famed for beauty. They loved to slip out in disguise for pleasure, and Xi did not stop them."

sentences.zh: 請謁必從，刑賞大政無不由之。

translations.literal: For audiences and petitions they always accompanied him; great matters of punishment and reward were none not decided by them.
translations.idiomatic: They attended every audience and petition. Punishment, reward, and every great affair passed through their hands."

sentences.zh: 初，昭儀有疾，龍城人王溫稱能療之，未幾而卒，熙忿其妄也，立於公車門支解溫而焚之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the lady of splendid beauty was ill, a man of Longcheng named Wang Wen claimed he could cure her; before long she died; Xi resented his falsehood and had Wen dismembered at the public carriage gate and burned.
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu fell ill, a Longcheng man named Wang Wen claimed he could heal her. She died soon after. Xi, furious at the lie, had Wen dismembered at the public gate and burned."

sentences.zh: 其後好游田，熙從之，北登白鹿山，東過青嶺，南臨滄海，百姓苦之，士卒為豺狼所害及凍死者五千餘人矣。

translations.literal: Afterward they loved the hunt; Xi followed them, climbing north to Bailu Mountain, passing east through Qing Ridge, facing south on the blue sea—the common people suffered bitterly, and soldiers killed by wolves or frozen to death numbered more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: They took to the hunt, and Xi went with them north to Bailu Mountain, east through Qing Ridge, and south to the sea. The people groaned under the burden. More than five thousand soldiers died by wolf or frost."

sentences.zh: 會高句驪寇燕郡，殺略百餘人。

translations.literal: It happened that Koguryŏ raided Yan commandery and killed and carried off more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Koguryŏ raided Yan commandery and killed or captured more than a hundred people."

sentences.zh: 熙伐高句驪，以苻氏從，為沖車地道以攻遼東。

translations.literal: Xi attacked Koguryŏ; the Fu lady accompanied him; he made battering rams and tunnels to attack Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: Xi marched on Koguryŏ with Lady Fu at his side, building rams and digging tunnels against Liaodong."

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「待剗平寇城，朕當與後乘輦而入，不聽將士先登。

translations.literal: Xi said, "When the bandit city is leveled, I shall enter in the rear carriage with the empress—I will not hear of the officers and soldiers climbing first.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "When the rebel city is level, I will enter in the rear carriage with the empress. I will not allow my men to climb the walls before us."

sentences.zh: 」於是城內嚴備，攻之不能下。

translations.literal: " Thereupon within the city they made strict preparations; the attack could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The city garrisoned in strength. The assault could not break it."

sentences.zh: 會大雨雪，士卒多死，乃引歸。

translations.literal: It happened that great rain and snow fell; many soldiers died, and he thereupon led the army back.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rain and snow fell. Many soldiers died, and he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 擬鄴之鳳陽門，作弘光門，累級三層。

translations.literal: Patterning himself on Ye's Fengyang Gate, he made the Hongguang Gate with three tiers of steps.
translations.idiomatic: He modeled the Hongguang Gate on Ye's Fengyang Gate, with three tiers of steps.

sentences.zh: 熙與苻氏襲契丹，憚其眾盛，將還，苻氏弗聽，遂棄輜重，輕襲高句驪，周行三千餘里，士馬疲凍，死者屬路。

translations.literal: Xi and Lady Fu attacked the Khitan. Fearful of their great numbers, they were about to return, but Lady Fu would not consent. They abandoned their baggage trains and made a light strike on Koguryŏ, marching a circuit of more than three thousand li. Men and horses were exhausted and frozen; the dead lined the road.
translations.idiomatic: Xi and Empress Fu marched against the Khitan. He wanted to turn back before their host, but she refused. They dropped their supply train and raided Koguryŏ on the fly, circling more than three thousand li until horses and men collapsed from cold and fatigue and corpses littered the route.

sentences.zh: 攻木底城，不克而還。

translations.literal: They attacked Mudi city but could not take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Mudi, failed to capture it, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 盡殺寶諸子。

translations.literal: He killed all of Bao's sons.
translations.idiomatic: He put every son of Murong Bao to death.

sentences.zh: 大城肥如及宿軍，以仇尼倪為鎮東大將軍、營州刺史，鎮宿軍，上庸公懿為鎮西將軍、幽州刺史，鎮令支；

translations.literal: He walled Feiru and Su Army Camp. He made Qiu Ni'ni Grand General Who Guards the East and governor of Ying Prefecture to garrison Su Army Camp, and Duke of Shangyong Yi Grand General Who Guards the West and governor of You Prefecture to garrison Lingzhi;
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Feiru and Su Army Camp, named Qiu Ni'ni Grand General Who Guards the East and governor of Ying to hold Su Army Camp, and Murong Yi, Duke of Shangyong, Grand General Who Guards the West and governor of You to hold Lingzhi;

sentences.zh: 尚書劉木為鎮南大將軍、冀州刺史，鎮肥如。

translations.literal: He made Liu Mu of the Masters of Writing Grand General Who Guards the South and governor of Ji Prefecture to garrison Feiru.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Mu of the Masters of Writing became Grand General Who Guards the South and governor of Ji, stationed at Feiru.

sentences.zh: 為苻氏起承華殿，高承光一倍，負土於北門，土與穀同價。

translations.literal: For Lady Fu he raised the Chenghua Hall, twice as high as Chengguang; earth was carried at the North Gate, and earth cost the same as grain.
translations.idiomatic: For Lady Fu he built the Chenghua Hall twice the height of Chengguang. Laborers hauled soil through the North Gate until dirt sold at grain prices.

sentences.zh: 典軍杜靜載棺詣闕，上書極諫。

translations.literal: The army inspector Du Jing brought a coffin to the palace gate and submitted a memorial of fierce remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jing, army inspector, arrived at the palace with a coffin on his cart and a memorial of desperate protest.

sentences.zh: 熙大怒，斬之。

translations.literal: Xi was greatly enraged and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Xi flew into a rage and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 苻氏嘗季夏思凍魚膾，仲冬須生地黃，皆下有司切責，不得，加以大辟，其虐也如此。

translations.literal: Lady Fu once in midsummer craved sliced raw frozen fish, and in midwinter demanded fresh rehmannia root; orders were sent down to the offices with stern demands, and when they could not obtain them she imposed capital punishment—such was her cruelty.
translations.idiomatic: In midsummer she wanted frozen fish sliced raw; in deep winter she demanded fresh rehmannia. Officials who failed to deliver were charged and, if they still could not comply, put to death. Her cruelty knew no limit.

sentences.zh: 苻氏死，熙悲號躃踴，若喪考妣，擁其屍而撫之曰：「體已就冷，命遂斷矣！

translations.literal: When Lady Fu died, Xi wailed and stamped in grief as though he had lost father and mother. He embraced her corpse and caressed it, saying, "The body has already grown cold; life is cut off!
translations.idiomatic: When Lady Fu died, Xi howled and stamped as if he had lost both parents. Clutching her corpse he stroked it and cried, "Your flesh is cold already; your breath is gone!

sentences.zh: 」於是僵僕氣絕，久而乃蘇。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stiffened and fell, breath ceased; only after a long while did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: He collapsed rigid and breathless, and only after a long while came back to himself.

sentences.zh: 大斂既訖，復啟其棺而與交接。

translations.literal: When the grand encoffinment was finished, he again opened the coffin and had intercourse with her.
translations.idiomatic: After the grand burial rites he opened the coffin again and lay with her body.

sentences.zh: 服斬縗，食粥。

translations.literal: He wore hemp mourning of the severest grade and ate gruel.
translations.idiomatic: He put on the deepest mourning garb and took only thin gruel.

sentences.zh: 制百僚于宮內哭臨，令沙門素服。

translations.literal: He ordered the hundred officials to mourn within the palace and commanded Buddhist monks to wear plain white.
translations.idiomatic: He made every minister weep inside the palace and ordered Buddhist monks into undyed robes.

sentences.zh: 使有司案檢哭者，有淚以為忠孝，無則罪之，於是群臣震懼，莫不含辛以為淚焉。

translations.literal: He had the offices examine those who wept; tears were taken as loyalty and filial piety, absence as crime. The ministers were struck with fear and all moistened their eyes with pungent juice to feign tears.
translations.idiomatic: Inspectors checked who wept. Tears meant loyalty; dry eyes meant punishment. Terrified, the court rubbed hot spices into their eyes until they wept on command.

sentences.zh: 慕容隆妻張氏，熙之嫂也，美姿容，有巧思。

translations.literal: Zhang, wife of Murong Long, was Xi's sister-in-law, beautiful in form and clever in mind.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, wife of Murong Long and Xi's sister-in-law, was lovely and quick-witted.

sentences.zh: 熙將以為苻氏之殉，欲以罪殺之，乃毀其禭靴，中有弊氈，遂賜死。

translations.literal: Xi intended her as a sacrifice companion for Lady Fu and wished to kill her on a pretext. He destroyed her lined boots and found worn felt inside; he thereupon granted her death.
translations.idiomatic: Xi meant to bury her alive with Lady Fu and needed a charge to kill her. He tore apart her lined boots, found shabby felt padding, and sentenced her to death.

sentences.zh: 三女叩頭求哀，熙不許。

translations.literal: Her three daughters knocked their heads begging mercy; Xi would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Her three daughters kowtowed and pleaded; Xi refused.

sentences.zh: 制公卿已下至於百姓，率戶營墓，費殫府藏。

translations.literal: He ordered from the highest ministers down to the common people that each household build the tomb; the expense emptied the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: From highest minister to commoner, every household had to build the tomb. The cost drained the treasury bare.

sentences.zh: 下錮三泉，周輸數里，內則圖畫尚書八坐之象。

translations.literal: Below were sealed three springs; the circuit ran several li; within were painted images of the eight directors of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Three springs were sealed beneath it; the ramparts ran for miles; inside, murals showed the eight seats of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 熙曰：「善為之，朕將隨後入此陵。

translations.literal: Xi said, "Make it well—I shall soon enter this tomb after.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Do your best. I will follow her into this mound soon.

sentences.zh: 」識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: Men of discernment took this as an ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard it called it a death omen.

sentences.zh: 其右僕射韋璆等並懼為殉，沐浴而待死焉。

translations.literal: The right vice director Wei Qiu and others all feared being sacrificed; they bathed and awaited death.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Qiu, right vice director, and others feared they would be buried alive. They bathed and waited for execution.

sentences.zh: 號苻氏墓曰征平陵。

translations.literal: He styled Lady Fu's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: He named Lady Fu's tomb Zhengping Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 熙被髮徒跣，步從苻氏喪。

translations.literal: Xi let down his hair and went barefoot, walking after Lady Fu's funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Xi went barefoot with loose hair, walking behind Lady Fu's bier.

sentences.zh: 轜車高大，毀北門而出。

translations.literal: The hearse was tall and great; the North Gate was destroyed to let it pass.
translations.idiomatic: The funeral carriage was so tall they had to smash the North Gate to get it out.

sentences.zh: 長老竊相謂曰：「慕容氏自毀其門，將不久也。」

translations.literal: The elders whispered to one another, "The Murong clan destroys its own gate—it will not be long."
translations.idiomatic: The elders murmured among themselves, "The Murong are tearing down their own house. They cannot last."

sentences.zh: 中衛將軍馮跋、左衛將軍張興，先皆坐事亡奔，以熙政之虐也，與跋從兄萬泥等二十二人結盟，推慕容雲為主，發尚方徒五千餘人閉門距守。

translations.literal: Central Guard General Feng Ba and Left Guard General Zhang Xing had earlier fled for offenses. Seeing Xi's cruel government, with Ba's cousin Wan Ni and twenty-two others they formed a covenant and made Murong Yun their leader, mobilizing more than five thousand convict laborers of the Palace Workshops to close the gates and resist.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba, Central Guard General, and Zhang Xing, Left Guard General, had already fled after criminal charges. Outraged by Xi's tyranny, Ba joined his cousin Wan Ni and twenty-one others to swear allegiance to Murong Yun. They rallied more than five thousand Palace Workshop convicts, shut the gates, and held the city.

sentences.zh: 中黃門趙洛生奔告之，熙曰：「此鼠盜耳，朕還當誅之。

translations.literal: The palace attendant Zhao Luosheng ran to report. Xi said, "These are mere rat-thieves—I shall return and execute them."
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Zhao Luosheng raced to tell him. Xi said, "Rats in a granary. I will be back to kill them."

sentences.zh: 」乃收發貫甲，馳還赴難。

translations.literal: He thereupon gathered weapons and armor, galloped back to meet the crisis.
translations.idiomatic: He armed his men, donned armor, and galloped home to crush the revolt.

sentences.zh: 夜至龍城，攻北門不克，遂敗，走入龍騰宛，微服隱于林中，為人所執，雲得而弑之，及其諸子同殯城北。

translations.literal: By night he reached Longcheng, attacked the North Gate but could not take it, was defeated, fled into the Longteng Garden, hid in the forest in plain dress, was seized by men. Yun got him and assassinated him, and his sons were buried together north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Longcheng at night, failed to break the North Gate, and fled to the Longteng Garden. Dressed as a commoner he hid in the woods, was caught, and Yun killed him. His sons were buried with him north of the city.

sentences.zh: 時年二十三，在位六年。

translations.literal: He was then twenty-three years old and had held the throne six years.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-three and had ruled six years.

sentences.zh: 雲葬之於苻氏墓，偽諡昭文皇帝。

translations.literal: Yun buried him in Lady Fu's tomb and gave the false posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Yun laid him in Lady Fu's tomb and gave him the posthumous title Emperor Zhaowen.

sentences.zh: 垂以孝武帝太元八年僭立，至熙四世，凡二十四年，以安帝義熙三年滅。

translations.literal: Chui had usurped the exalted title in the eighth year of Emperor Xiaowu's Taiyuan era; to Xi was four generations, altogether twenty-four years; it perished in the third year of Emperor An's Yixi era.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui seized the throne in Taiyuan year eight of Emperor Xiaowu. Four generations later, at Xi, the line had lasted twenty-four years. It fell in Yixi year three of Emperor An.

sentences.zh: 初，童謠曰：「一束槁，兩頭然，禿頭小兒來滅燕。

translations.literal: Earlier a children's rhyme said, "One bundle of straw, both ends burning—a bald-headed little boy will come to destroy Yan."
translations.idiomatic: A children's rhyme had once said, "A bundle of straw with both ends lit—a bald-headed boy will end Yan."

sentences.zh: 」槁字上有草，下有禾，兩頭然則禾草俱盡而成高字。

translations.literal: The character for straw has grass above and grain below; when both ends burn, grain and grass are both consumed and it becomes the character gao.
translations.idiomatic: The word for straw stacks grass over grain. Burn both ends and grass and grain vanish, leaving the character for "Gao."

sentences.zh: 雲父名拔，小字禿頭，三子，而雲季也。

translations.literal: Yun's father was named Ba, his childhood name Bald Head; he had three sons, and Yun was the youngest.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's father was called Ba, nicknamed Bald Head. He had three sons; Yun was the youngest.

sentences.zh: 熙竟為雲所滅，如謠言焉。

translations.literal: Xi was indeed destroyed by Yun, as the rhyme said.
translations.idiomatic: Xi fell to Yun exactly as the rhyme foretold.

sentences.zh: 慕容雲，字子雨，寶之養子也。

translations.literal: Murong Yun, courtesy name Ziyu, was Bao's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yun, styled Ziyu, was the adopted son of Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 祖父和，高句驪之支庶，自雲高陽氏之苗裔，故以高為氏焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather He was a collateral branch of Koguryŏ; claiming descent from the house of Gaoyang, they took Gao as their surname.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather He came from a Koguryŏ collateral line. The family claimed descent from Gaoyang and took Gao as their surname.

sentences.zh: 雲沈深有局量，厚重希言，時人咸以為愚，唯馮跋奇其志度而友之。

translations.literal: Yun was deep and reserved with great capacity, weighty and sparing in speech; contemporaries all thought him foolish—only Feng Ba marveled at his ambition and befriended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was grave, patient, and slow to speak. Most men thought him a fool. Only Feng Ba saw his resolve and made him a friend.

sentences.zh: 寶之為太子，雲以武藝給事侍東宮，拜侍御郎，襲敗慕容會軍。

translations.literal: When Bao was crown prince, Yun served the Eastern Palace by martial arts, was appointed attendant cavalier, and raided and defeated Murong Hui's army.
translations.idiomatic: While Bao was crown prince, Yun served the Eastern Palace for his fighting skill, became attendant cavalier, and routed Murong Hui's force in a raid.

sentences.zh: 寶子之，賜姓慕容氏，封夕陽公。

translations.literal: Bao adopted him as son, granted the surname Murong, and enfeoffed him as Duke of Xiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Bao adopted him, gave him the Murong surname, and enfeoffed him Duke of Xiyang.

sentences.zh: 熙之葬苻氏也，馮跋詣雲，告之以謀。

translations.literal: When Xi was burying Lady Fu, Feng Ba went to Yun and told him the plan.
translations.idiomatic: During Lady Fu's funeral, Feng Ba came to Yun and laid out the plot.

sentences.zh: 雲懼曰：「吾嬰疾歷年，卿等所知，願更圖之。

translations.literal: Yun said in fear, "I have been ill for years, as you know—please devise another plan."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said in alarm, "You know I have been sick for years. Find someone else."

sentences.zh: 」跋逼曰：「慕容氏世衰，河間虐暴，惑妖淫之女而逆亂天常，百姓不堪其害，思亂者十室九焉，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Ba pressed him, saying, "The Murong house declines generation by generation. The Prince of Hejian is cruel and violent, deluded by a demon harlot and perverting heaven's constant way. The people cannot bear the harm; in nine of ten households they think of rebellion. This is the hour when heaven destroys them."
translations.idiomatic: Ba pressed on: "The Murong line is spent. Xi of Hejian is savage, bewitched by a witch, and has overturned heaven's order. The people are broken—nine houses in ten want revolt. Heaven itself is ending them."

sentences.zh: 公自高氏名家，何能為他養子！

translations.literal: You are from the famous house of Gao—how can you remain another man's adopted son!
translations.idiomatic: You are of the great house of Gao. How long will you play another man's son?

sentences.zh: 機運難邀，千歲一時，公焉得辭也！

translations.literal: Opportunity is hard to summon—once in a thousand years—how can you decline!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune comes once in a thousand years. You cannot refuse it!

sentences.zh: 」扶之而出。

translations.literal: He supported him and brought him out.
translations.idiomatic: They lifted him up and marched him out.

sentences.zh: 雲曰：「吾疾苦日久，廢絕世務。

translations.literal: Yun said, "My illness has long been grave; I have abandoned worldly affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Yun said, "I have been sick too long and have left the world behind."

sentences.zh: 卿今興建大事，謬見推逼。

translations.literal: You now raise a great affair and mistakenly press me forward.
translations.idiomatic: You are launching a great enterprise and wrongly force me to lead it.

sentences.zh: 所以徘徊，非為身也，實惟否德不足以濟元元故耳。

translations.literal: The reason I hesitate is not for myself—it is truly that my lacking virtue is insufficient to deliver the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: I hesitate not for my own sake but because I lack the virtue to save the people.

sentences.zh: 」跋等強之，雲遂即天王位，復姓高氏，大赦境內殊死以下，改元曰正始，國號大燕。

translations.literal: Ba and others forced him; Yun thereupon assumed the title of Heavenly King, restored the surname Gao, granted amnesty within the realm short of death, changed the era name to Zhengshi, and styled the state Great Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ba and the rest would not relent. Yun took the title Heavenly King, resumed the surname Gao, declared amnesty short of death, named the era Zhengshi, and called the state Great Yan.

sentences.zh: 署馮跋侍中、都督中外諸軍事、征北大將軍、開府儀同三司、錄尚書事、武邑公，封伯、子、男，鄉、亭侯者五十餘人，士卒賜穀帛有差。

translations.literal: He appointed Feng Ba palace attendant, commander-in-chief of all armies at home and abroad, grand general who campaigns north, commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Marquis of Wuyi; he enfeoffed more than fifty as counts, viscounts, barons, and township and village marquises; soldiers received grain and silk in differing amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba became palace attendant, supreme commander, Grand General Who Campaigns North, commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies, recorder of the Masters of Writing, and Marquis of Wuyi. More than fifty men received ranks from count down to village marquis. Soldiers were paid grain and cloth by rank.

sentences.zh: 熙之群官，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Xi's whole corps of officials had their ranks restored.
translations.idiomatic: Every officer who had served Xi had his title restored.

sentences.zh: 立妻李氏為天王後，子彭為太子。

translations.literal: He established his wife Lady Li as Heavenly Queen and his son Peng as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: He made his wife Lady Li Heavenly Queen and his son Peng crown prince.

sentences.zh: 越騎校尉慕輿良謀叛，雲誅之。

translations.literal: The Colonel of Rapid Cavalry Murong Liang plotted rebellion; Yun executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Liang, Colonel of Rapid Cavalry, plotted treason. Yun had him killed.

sentences.zh: 雲臨東堂，幸臣離班、桃仁懷劍執紙而入，稱有所啟，拔劍擊雲，雲以幾距班，桃仁進而弑之。

translations.literal: Yun was at the Eastern Hall. His favored attendants Li Ban and Tao Ren entered with swords concealed, holding paper and claiming to report; they drew swords and struck Yun. Yun used a table to block Ban; Tao Ren advanced and assassinated him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun sat in the Eastern Hall. His favorites Li Ban and Tao Ren came in with swords hidden, papers in hand, claiming a report. They drew and struck. Yun blocked Ban with a table; Tao Ren stepped in and killed him.

sentences.zh: 馮跋遷雲屍於東宮，偽諡惠懿皇帝。

translations.literal: Feng Ba moved Yun's corpse to the Eastern Palace and gave the false posthumous title Emperor Huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ba moved Yun's body to the Eastern Palace and posthumously named him Emperor Huiyi.

sentences.zh: 雲自以無功德而為豪桀所推，常內懷懼，故寵養壯士以為腹心。

translations.literal: Yun, knowing he had no merit yet was pushed forward by the bold, inwardly always feared; therefore he favored and nurtured stalwarts as his inner confidants.
translations.idiomatic: Yun knew he had done nothing to earn the throne and had been raised by strongmen. He lived in fear and kept fierce warriors close as his private guard.

sentences.zh: 離班、桃仁等並專典禁衛，委之以爪牙之任，賞賜月至數千萬，衣食臥起皆與之同，終以此致敗雲。

translations.literal: Li Ban, Tao Ren, and others all exclusively controlled the palace guard; he entrusted them with fang-and-claw duties; rewards and gifts reached tens of millions each month; eating, clothing, sleeping, and rising were all with them—at last by this Yun was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ban, Tao Ren, and their circle ran the palace guard alone. He gave them the work of fangs and claws. They received tens of millions in gifts each month and ate, dressed, and slept at his side. In the end they killed him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：四星東聚，金陵之氣已分；

translations.literal: The historian writes: Four stars gathered in the east; the aura of Jinling was already divided;
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Four stars clustered in the east, and the fortune of Jinling had already split.

sentences.zh: 五馬南浮，玉塞之雄方擾。

translations.literal: Five horses floated south; the heroes of the Jade Frontier were just then in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: Five horses drifted south while the champions of the Jade Pass stirred in disorder.

sentences.zh: 市朝屢改，艱虞靡息。

translations.literal: Markets and courts changed repeatedly; hardship and peril never ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Thrones and markets turned over again and again, and trouble never rested.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂天資英傑，威震本朝，以雄略見猜而庇身寬政，永固受之而以禮，道明事之而畢力。

translations.literal: Murong Chui was gifted by nature with heroic excellence, his might shaking the age; suspected for his bold strategy he sheltered himself under tolerant rule; Yong received him with courtesy, and Daoming served him with full exertion.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui was a born hero whose power shook his own age. Distrusted for his ambition, he took refuge under a lenient court. Murong Yong welcomed him with ritual; Murong Daoming served him with everything he had.

sentences.zh: 然而隼質難羈，狼心自野。

translations.literal: Yet the falcon's nature is hard to tether; the wolf's heart runs wild of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a falcon cannot be leashed forever, and a wolf's heart answers only to the wild.

sentences.zh: 淮南失律，三甥之謀已構；

translations.literal: At Huainan the laws of war were lost—the three nephews' plot was already formed;
translations.idiomatic: At Huainan he broke the rules of war, and the three nephews' conspiracy was already in motion.

sentences.zh: 河朔分麾，五木之祥雲啟。

translations.literal: North of the River the standards divided—the auspice of the Five Woods opened in the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yellow River the banners split apart, and the omen of the Five Woods rose in the clouds.

sentences.zh: 斬飛龍而遐舉，逾石門而長邁，遂使翟氏景從，鄴師宵逸，收羅趙、魏，驅駕英雄。

translations.literal: He slew the flying dragon and rose afar, crossed Shimen and marched on—thereby making the Zhai clan follow like a shadow, the Ye army flee by night, gathering Zhao and Wei, driving heroes before him.
translations.idiomatic: He cut down the flying dragon and soared away, crossed Shimen and pressed on, drew the Zhai house after him like a shadow, sent the Ye garrison fleeing by night, gathered Zhao and Wei, and drove heroes before his chariot.

sentences.zh: 叩囊餘奇，摧五萬于河曲；

translations.literal: Knocking the bag's remaining marvels, he shattered fifty thousand at the river bend;
translations.idiomatic: He tapped the last wonders in his satchel and broke fifty thousand men on the river bend.

sentences.zh: 浮船秘策，招七郡于黎陽。

translations.literal: Floating-boat secret plans drew seven commanderies at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: With secret plans carried on floating boats he won seven commanderies at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 返遼陰之舊物，創中山之新社，類帝禋宗，僭擬斯備。

translations.literal: He recovered old lands in Liaoyin, founded a new altar-state at Zhongshan—rites like the Emperor's, usurpation complete.
translations.idiomatic: He reclaimed the old domain in Liaoyin, built a new state altar at Zhongshan, and matched imperial rites until his pretense was complete.

sentences.zh: 夫以重耳歸晉，賴五臣之功；

translations.literal: As for Chong'er returning to Jin, it relied on the merit of the five ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When Chong'er returned to Jin, he needed the five loyal ministers.

sentences.zh: 句踐紿吳，資五千之卒。

translations.literal: Goujian deceived Wu with five thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: Goujian fooled Wu with an army of five thousand.

sentences.zh: 惡有業殊二霸，眾微一旅，掎拔而傾山嶽，騰嘯而禦風雲！

translations.literal: How could there be an enterprise unlike the two hegemons, a multitude slight as one brigade, prying up and toppling mountains, leaping and roaring to ride the wind and clouds!
translations.idiomatic: What feat could match the two hegemons—one thin column prying mountains over, roaring up to ride the wind and clouds!

sentences.zh: 雖衛人忘亡復傳于東國，任好余裕伊愧於西鄰，信苻氏之奸回，非晉室之鯨鯢矣。

translations.literal: Though the men of Wei forgot extinction and passed the line eastward, and Duke Mu of Qin had leisure to feel shame before his western neighbor—it is credible that Fu Jian's house was treacherous, not the leviathan of the Jin court.
translations.idiomatic: Wei forgot it was dying and passed its line east; Duke Mu of Qin had room to blush before his western neighbor. The Fu clan were rogues, not the great whale of Jin.

sentences.zh: 寶以浮譽獲升，峻文禦俗，蕭牆內憤，勍敵外陵，雖毒不被物而惡足自剿。

translations.literal: Bao rose on floating reputation, governed the people with harsh statutes; fury raged within the palace wall, fierce foes pressed from without—though poison did not touch others, how could it spare himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bao climbed on empty fame and ruled with harsh law. Rage festered inside the palace; strong enemies closed in from without. Poison that spares others still poisons the hand that holds it.

sentences.zh: 盛則孝友冥符，文武不墜，韜光而夷仇賊，罪己而遜高危，翩翩然濁世之佳虜矣。

translations.literal: Sheng then: filial piety and brotherhood matched in mystery, civil and martial arts unbroken; he hid his light and pacified enemies, blamed himself and yielded high peril—gracefully the finest captive of a troubled age.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng matched filial duty with brotherly care, kept both civil and martial arts alive, hid his brilliance to humble foes, blamed himself and stepped back from danger—the finest hostage a broken age could produce.

sentences.zh: 熙乃地非奧主，舉因淫德。

translations.literal: Xi: the land was no domain for a hidden lord; his rise was altogether through licentious virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was no secret sage for the throne. He won it through lust alone.

sentences.zh: 驪戎之態，取悅于匡床；

translations.literal: The manner of Li Rong pleased on the nuptial couch;
translations.idiomatic: He had the allure of Li Rong on the marriage bed.

sentences.zh: 玄妻之姿，見奇於鬒發。

translations.literal: The beauty of Xuan's wife was marveled at for her black hair.
translations.idiomatic: He prized a beauty like Xuan's wife for her dark hair.

sentences.zh: 蕩輕舟于曲光之海，望朝涉于景雲之山，飾土木於驕心，窮怨嗟於蕞壤，宗祀夷滅，為馮氏之驅除焉。

translations.literal: He drifted light boats on the Quguang Sea, gazed on the morning ford from Jingyun Mountain, adorned earth and timber to feed arrogant hearts, exhausted lament on the smallest soil—the ancestral sacrifices were extinguished, and he became what the Feng clan swept away.
translations.idiomatic: He sailed light boats on the Quguang Sea, watched the morning crossing from Jingyun Mountain, piled earth and timber to please his pride, and wrung the land dry with groans until the ancestral rites were gone and the Feng house swept him aside.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：戎狄憑陵，山川沸騰。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Rong and Di pressed upon the borders; mountains and rivers boiled.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium says: Barbarians overran the frontiers; mountains and rivers seethed.

sentences.zh: 天未悔禍，人非與能。

translations.literal: Heaven had not yet repented of calamity; men were not those who could match it.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had not yet turned from disaster, and no man was equal to the hour.

sentences.zh: 疾走而捷，先鳴則興。

translations.literal: Swift running brings triumph; he who calls first rises.
translations.idiomatic: Run fast and you win; cry first and you rise.

sentences.zh: 道明烈烈，鞭笞豪傑。

translations.literal: Daoming blazed fiercely, lashing the bold.
translations.idiomatic: Daoming burned bright and whipped the heroes into line.

sentences.zh: 掃燕夷魏，釗屠永滅。

translations.literal: He swept Yan, leveled Wei, carved and slaughtered until Yong was ended.
translations.idiomatic: He scoured Yan, crushed Wei, cut and killed until Yong was gone.

sentences.zh: 大盜潛移，鴻名遂竊。

translations.literal: The great thief shifted in secret; the vast name was stolen.
translations.idiomatic: The great robber moved in the dark and stole the lofty name.

sentences.zh: 寶心生亂，盛清家難。

translations.literal: Bao bred disorder in the heart; Sheng cleared the family's tribulation.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sowed chaos at home; Sheng eased the clan's calamity.

sentences.zh: 熙極驕淫，人懷憤惋。

translations.literal: Xi reached the extreme of arrogance and lust; men harbored resentment and grief.
translations.idiomatic: Xi drowned in pride and lust until every heart burned with anger and grief.

sentences.zh: 孽貽身咎，災無以逭。

translations.literal: Evil legacy brought bodily doom; disaster could not be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His crimes clung to his flesh; no calamity could be outrun.
